articles.title: Eisenkot warns of Israel crisis as he seeks to replace Netanyahu’s government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: isenkot, 66, a political novice who has vowed to bridge Israel's deep polarisation under Netanyahu, formally received a mandate from President Isaac Herzog, giving him 28 days to form a government despite his bloc lacking a clear majority

Israel's former military chief Gadi Eisenkot started the tough task on Sunday (November 8, 2026) of forming a government , reaching out to Benjamin Netanyahu's allies as he warned the veteran Prime Minister had brought the country to a historic crisis.

Mr. Eisenkot, 66, a political novice who has vowed to bridge Israel's deep polarisation under Mr. Netanyahu, formally received a mandate from President Isaac Herzog, giving him 28 days to form a government despite his bloc lacking a clear majority.

"We are in a state of emergency, approaching a point of no return for the State of Israel," Mr. Eisenkot, who had traded his usual all black for a suit and tie, said at a ceremony at the Presidential office.
"We must form a national emergency government. This will require creative and unconventional political steps."

Mr. Eisenkot, born to a family of working-class Moroccan immigrants, would be the first Sephardic Prime Minister — a community mostly descended from West Asian or North African Jews — in a country long dominated by an Ashkenazi elite with ties to Europe.

Mr. Netanyahu is Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister, having led the country on and off for nearly two decades. He has taken the country in a sharply rightward direction and led wars in Gaza, Lebanon, and Iran since the October 7, 2023, attacks by Hamas.
Both Mr. Eisenkot and Mr. Herzog acknowledged Israel's growing isolation under Mr. Netanyahu, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court.

In the United States, the most vital ally of Israel, Democrats on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) swept elections with calls to rein in Israel after the devastation in Gaza and the unpopular Iran war which Mr. Netanyahu launched with President Donald Trump.
"We are in the midst of a devastating diplomatic crisis. Even our closest friends and strategic allies are saying their relationship with Israel must be reassessed," Mr. Eisenkot said.
Mr. Eisenkot appealed to Mr. Netanyahu's Likud Party as well as the far-right party of Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich to join — but only with himself as Prime Minister.
"My door is open and my hand is extended, wholeheartedly and willingly, to anyone who understands the gravity of this moment," he said.
In consultations last week with Mr. Herzog, Mr. Eisenkot received recommendations from parties accounting for 67 lawmakers, against 46 for Mr. Netanyahu.

articles.title: South Africa's ANC suffers worst election result as decline continues
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The once-dominant ANC — the party of Nelson Mandela — had received around 30% of the vote in Wednesday's (November 4, 2026) local government elections with 99% of ballots counted

South Africa's African National Congress party faced its worst election results ever on Sunday (November 8, 2026) and a new low point on its gradual decline in popularity as voters rebuked it for a failure to deliver basic services like water and electricity in towns and cities.

The once-dominant ANC — the party of Nelson Mandela — had received around 30% of the vote in Wednesday's (November 4, 2026) local government elections with 99% of ballots counted. The final results were expected late on Sunday (November 8, 2026), according to the Independent Electoral Commission.

The ANC remained the largest party by total share in an election involving hundreds of parties, but the Democratic Alliance that is its main Opposition had received around 25% of votes in the near-complete count.

That brought closer to reality the once-unthinkable notion that the ANC that led South Africa out of the white minority rule of apartheid and delivered freedom in 1994 under Mandela might one day not be its biggest party. It used to command 70% of the vote.

The ANC's popularity has declined for more than a decade. It won 45% support in the last local elections in 2021, the first time it had dropped below 50% in any election. In 2024, it then lost its Parliamentary majority for the first time in a national election, which brought about a coalition national government and a seismic shift in South African politics.

The ANC was on course Sunday (November 8, 2026) for a steep drop of about 15 percentage points from the last local elections and the loss of approximately one-third of its support from five years ago.
“If anyone has not heard what the people are saying in this election, then you are lost,” said ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula. “This has been a very catastrophic outcome for the ANC.”
He said the results called for the ANC “to be humble, to hear our people and respect them,” and to “earn again through service and not through slogans the trust people have lent to others.”
DA leader Geordin Hill-Lewis said his party — which was around 20% points behind the ANC in the 2024 national election — had now “taken a big step forward” in its aim to be South Africa's biggest.
But, while the ANC's popularity has dropped sharply, no single party has overtaken it as the vote has fragmented among many parties on a local and national scale.

Another seven major parties shared around 30% of the vote in these local elections, which had more than 500 parties contesting and many picking up small shares. The MK Party led by former South African President Jacob Zuma, who broke away from the ANC and was expelled by it, held the third-largest share of votes at around 10%.

Voters across South Africa have long expressed frustration over failed public services that have left many cities and towns with regular water and electricity outages, broken roads and streetlights, and uncollected refuse.

articles.title: Trump vows comeback as bitter showdown with Congress looms
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The devastating result leaves Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year 'lame duck' period of his White House tenure

U.S. President Donald Trump vowed a political comeback on Sunday (November 8, 2026) after his Republican Party lost control of both houses of Congress in midterm elections that amounted to an unequivocal repudiation of his turbulent Presidency.

The devastating result leaves Mr. Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year 'lame duck' period of his White House tenure, while opening the door to multiple investigations by the Democrat-controlled Congress into the President, his family and senior members of his administration.

"America took a giant step back in History with the results of the last Election," Mr. Trump said in a post on Truth Social, adding that the stock market that had grown during his tenure took a loss after the vote.
"But have no fear, we will be back, BIGGER AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE!"
While the resounding election loss last Tuesday (November 3, 2026) has prompted soul-searching among Republican lawmakers, Mr. Trump has sounded defiant.
On Friday (November 6, 2026), he appointed hardline advisor Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff, signalling a bare-knuckle fightback.
Democrats, meanwhile, have pledged to hold the Trump administration to account and fight against Mr. Miller, the architect of Mr. Trump's tough immigration policy.

Amid Democrat threats for administration officials to "lawyer up," Mr. Trump said on Saturday (November 8, 2026) he was ordering the Justice Department to examine Democratic threats to impeach members of his administration, likening it to "extortion."
That stance stoked a war of words between top Republicans and Democrats on U.S. political shows on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
Attorney General Todd Blanche, a former personal lawyer for Mr. Trump and now head of the Justice Department, vowed to actively defend Mr. Trump and senior members of his administration.

"You have members of Congress who, after Tuesday (November 3, 2026), have done nothing but threaten everything that's happening in this administration," Mr. Blanche told CNN , citing impeachment threats against Mr. Miller after his appointment.
"If they try to come after Stephen Miller...instead of actually just conducting oversight and leading, of course the Department of Justice will be there to defend him."

articles.title: Thick smog blankets Delhi on Deepavali night, AQI at 20 stations ‘severe’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Air Quality Early Warning System (EWS) has forecast that Delhi's air quality is likely to slip into the 'severe' category from November 9 and remain there for the subsequent few days

A smoky haze hung over Delhi on Deepavali night, blurring streetlights and blanketing neighbourhoods as celebrations intensified across the capital, pushing air quality at 20 monitoring stations into the ‘severe’ category, with the overall Air Quality Index standing at 371 at 10 p.m..

The haze grew denser as the evening progressed, with smoke from firecrackers hanging over roads and residential neighbourhoods. The smell of burnt crackers lingered in the air, while visibility dropped in several parts of the capital and residents reported difficulty breathing.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Delhi air pollution: Capital sees ‘very poor’ AQI on Deepavali as GRAP 3 curbs continue

Despite restrictions on bursting firecrackers, several parts of Delhi continued to witness their use on Sunday evening (November 8, 2026), with reports of fireworks emerging from areas, including Pitampura, Burari, Mayur Vihar and parts of Lutyens’ Delhi.
Ahead of Deepavali, the Delhi government had appealed to people to comply with the Supreme Court’s directions on sale and use of green firecrackers.
The District Magistrate (East), in an order, had permitted the bursting of green firecrackers only on November 7 and 8, between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and 8 p.m. and 10 p.m..

Residents reported that firecrackers were being burst in outer Delhi’s Pitampura and Burari, with the intensity particularly high in Burari. Similar reports came from Mayur Vihar, while people in the Bishambardas Marg area and Lutyens’ Delhi said fireworks continued, although the intensity had reduced slightly.

Of the 59 monitoring stations, 19 were in the 'severe' category at 7 p.m., seven in the 'poor' category, and the remaining 33 in the 'very poor' category. Jahangirpuri recorded the highest AQI at 460.
The city's average AQI for the day settled at 376 in the 'very poor' category, compared to 369 on Saturday, amid a layer of smog and reduced visibility.
The court prohibited bursting of firecrackers within 300 metres of hospitals, nursing homes, health centres, old-age homes, educational institutions and other notified silence zones.

Only CSIR-NEERI-certified green firecrackers were permitted for sale, with the administration directing that they be sold exclusively at locations designated by the Delhi Police. The administration had also announced joint patrolling and enforcement teams comprising district officials and Delhi Police personnel to check unauthorised sale and use of prohibited firecrackers.
Meanwhile, the Air Quality Early Warning System (EWS) has forecast that Delhi's air quality is likely to slip into the 'severe' category from November 9 and remain there for the subsequent few days.

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

The Air Quality Early Warning System (EWS) has forecast that Delhi's air quality is likely to slip into the 'severe' category from November 9 and remain there for the subsequent few days

A smoky haze hung over Delhi on Deepavali night, blurring streetlights and blanketing neighbourhoods as celebrations intensified across the capital, pushing air quality at 20 monitoring stations into the ‘severe’ category, with the overall Air Quality Index standing at 371 at 10 p.m..

The haze grew denser as the evening progressed, with smoke from firecrackers hanging over roads and residential neighbourhoods. The smell of burnt crackers lingered in the air, while visibility dropped in several parts of the capital and residents reported difficulty breathing.

ALSO WATCH Watch: Delhi air pollution: Capital sees ‘very poor’ AQI on Deepavali as GRAP 3 curbs continue

Despite restrictions on bursting firecrackers, several parts of Delhi continued to witness their use on Sunday evening (November 8, 2026), with reports of fireworks emerging from areas, including Pitampura, Burari, Mayur Vihar and parts of Lutyens’ Delhi.

Ahead of Deepavali, the Delhi government had appealed to people to comply with the Supreme Court’s directions on sale and use of green firecrackers.

The District Magistrate (East), in an order, had permitted the bursting of green firecrackers only on November 7 and 8, between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and 8 p.m. and 10 p.m..

Residents reported that firecrackers were being burst in outer Delhi’s Pitampura and Burari, with the intensity particularly high in Burari. Similar reports came from Mayur Vihar, while people in the Bishambardas Marg area and Lutyens’ Delhi said fireworks continued, although the intensity had reduced slightly.

Of the 59 monitoring stations, 19 were in the 'severe' category at 7 p.m., seven in the 'poor' category, and the remaining 33 in the 'very poor' category. Jahangirpuri recorded the highest AQI at 460.

The city's average AQI for the day settled at 376 in the 'very poor' category, compared to 369 on Saturday, amid a layer of smog and reduced visibility.

The court prohibited bursting of firecrackers within 300 metres of hospitals, nursing homes, health centres, old-age homes, educational institutions and other notified silence zones.

Only CSIR-NEERI-certified green firecrackers were permitted for sale, with the administration directing that they be sold exclusively at locations designated by the Delhi Police. The administration had also announced joint patrolling and enforcement teams comprising district officials and Delhi Police personnel to check unauthorised sale and use of prohibited firecrackers.

Meanwhile, the Air Quality Early Warning System (EWS) has forecast that Delhi's air quality is likely to slip into the 'severe' category from November 9 and remain there for the subsequent few days.

articles.title: AIDSO protests in Kalaburagi and Ballari against proposed closure of 45,000 government schools
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The All India Democratic Students’ Organisation (AIDSO) staged protests in Kalaburagi and Ballari on Friday, opposing the Karnataka government’s proposed KPS Magnet school policy, which the organisation alleged would lead to the closure of around 45,000 government schools across the State.

The protests were held at Thimmapur Circle in Kalaburagi and OPD Circle in Ballari. The demonstrators condemned the Congress government for allegedly moving ahead with the policy despite strong public opposition and demanded that it withdraw the proposal and protect the public education system.

Addressing the protesters in Kalaburagi, AIDSO district president Tuljaram N.K. alleged that the government, which had promised to protect government schools before coming to power, was now preparing to close thousands of them in the name of the KPS Magnet scheme and implement the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020. He claimed that the conditions mentioned in the loan agreement with the Asian Development Bank (ADB) clearly indicated the proposed changes.
AIDSO activists staging a protest at OPD Circle in Ballari on Friday, opposing the proposed closure of 45,000 government schools under the KPS Magnet scheme. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

AIDSO State treasurer Subhash Bettadakoppa, speaking at the Ballari protest, also criticised the government for allegedly accepting conditions that would undermine the public education system. He questioned how the Congress could claim to be protecting democracy while pursuing a policy that, according to the organisation, would deprive children from poor families of access to government schools.

The speakers alleged that the ADB-linked conditions envisaged the merger of all government schools around school clusters into a single institution by 2030; financial support from corporate companies for the management of KPS Magnet schools; and a curriculum designed to prepare students as a workforce suited to the needs of those companies. They also claimed that future teacher recruitment would be restricted to KPS schools and that the government would stop providing grants to these schools after 2030.

The protesters expressed concern that the policy would leave only 4,038 schools functioning in Karnataka while resulting in the closure of around 45,000 government schools. They alleged that the State’s education policy was increasingly being shaped by foreign financial institutions and corporate interests rather than by educationists and intellectuals from Karnataka.

Abdul Waheed, president of the district committee for the protection of public education, also addressed the Kalaburagi protest. In Ballari, S.G. Nagarathna, vice-president of the committee, said the proposed policy posed a serious threat to public education and called for a united struggle to protect government schools.

Referring to the 200th birth anniversary of social reformer Jyotiba Phule, the speakers said protecting public education was a historic responsibility and warned that the organisation would intensify its agitation against the policy.

The Kalaburagi protest was presided over by AIDSO district secretary Venkatesh Devadurga. District vice-presidents Radha Preeti Doddamani and Govind Yalawar, Nagaraj Ravoor, and other members and activists participated.

In Ballari, the protest was presided over by district secretary Kambali Manjunath. AIDSO district president K. Eranna, vice-president M. Shanthi, district treasurer Anupama, office secretary Niharika, members Kantesh and Thippeswamy, and hundreds of students took part.

articles.title: Fire breaks out at high-rise building in Mumbai’s Ghatkopar East; three hospitalised
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ganesh Shinde said that the fire started while the residents were using a drill to install fairy lights in their house for Deepavali, which triggered the short circuit
Three people, including two children, were hospitalised after a fire broke out on one floor of a 25-storey residential building in Ghatkopar East on Friday evening (November 6, 2026).

The fire has been brought under control, with the police suspecting a short circuit as the preliminary cause of the blaze. No fatalities have been reported and the condition of all three in the hospital was reported to be stable.
According to a statement issued by the Mayor’s Office, the Mumbai Fire Brigade, the entire building was evacuated as a precautionary measure.

Three people were reported injured in the incident. According to an update received from the on-duty Assistant Medical Officer (AMO) at 9.25 p.m., Sainath Awale (45) sustained 27% burn injuries and was reported to be in stable condition. Meanwhile, Dr. Rozbin of Zynova Hospital confirmed at 10.40 p.m. that two other injured persons, identified as Nirav Lodaya (34) and Rajesh Lodaya (47), had been admitted to the hospital. Both were reported to be in stable condition.

The incident occurred on the 23rd floor of the Royal Altezza building on Vallabh Baug Lane in Pant Nagar. According to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), the Mumbai Fire Brigade (MFB) received information about the blaze at 8.08 p.m.
The fire brigade initially declared a Level-I fire call at 8.30 p.m, which was subsequently escalated to Level-II at 8.52 p.m.

Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde visited the site on Friday night (November 6, 2026) and reviewed the ongoing rescue and relief operations. Local MLA Parag Shah and corporators Suresh Awale and Dharmesh Giri were also present at the spot.

DCP (East Zone 2) Ganesh Shinde said that the fire started while the residents were using a drill to install fairy lights in their house for Deepavali, which triggered the short circuit. Now, the building will be shut till the Fire Department and the Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited ask to reopen. The residents were requested to get food to eat and stay with neighbours or family in the city for the night.
After safety and security checks by the Mumbai Fire Brigade and the Mumbai police, wings C and D of the building were cleared for residents to return to.
According to the Chief Fire Officer, the blaze has been brought under control. One injured person was shifted to Rajawadi Hospital, where their condition was reported to be stable.
Two children who suffered from suffocation were taken to Zynova Hospital.
Personnel from the Mumbai Fire Brigade, police, the electricity distribution company, the Public Works Department (PWD) and the BMC’s ward staff were mobilised following the incident.

articles.title: Students urged to explore opportunities beyond conventional career paths
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Students must take ownership of their careers, identify their strengths, and continuously upgrade skills to succeed in an evolving professional landscape, say speakers at a career seminar organised by The Hindu FIC

Students must take ownership of their careers, identify their strengths and aspirations, and continuously upgrade their skills to succeed in an evolving professional landscape, said Prof. Satya Duvvuri of the Paari School of Business, SRM University-AP.

Addressing students at a seminar on ‘Career Opportunities in Management & Technology’, organised by The Hindu FIC and Paari School of Business, SRM AP, he urged them to explore opportunities beyond conventional career paths and make informed choices driven by their interests and determination.

Through real-life examples, anecdotes and interactive discussions, Prof. Satya highlighted how several successful professionals from engineering and science backgrounds had utilised their technical knowledge to emerge as prominent leaders in diverse fields.
He emphasised that passion, perseverance and a willingness to learn could open doors to limitless career opportunities.
Logo for The Hindu FIC & SRM AP seminar on careers in management and technology

He underlined the growing importance of analytical thinking, comprehension and proficiency in emerging technologies, particularly Artificial Intelligence (AI), in preparing students for future careers. Encouraging them to dream big, work hard and pursue their passions, he said opportunities were often closer than they imagined and that their future depended largely on their own choices and efforts.

Executive Director of Kallam Haranadhareddy Institute of Technology (KHIT) Navya Kallam said that the world offered opportunities across diverse sectors and that engineering graduates could explore areas beyond their core disciplines.
She pointed out that skills such as accounting, which is considered the backbone of any business, could help students become successful entrepreneurs.
KHIT Director Uma Shankar Reddy observed that there was no age limit for acquiring new skills.

Citing the example of the institution’s founder K. Haranadhareddy, who learnt music at the age of 75 and performed at temples, he encouraged students to remain open to learning throughout their lives. He also stressed that higher educational qualifications could strengthen career prospects, noting that additional qualifications often offered an advantage in career advancement and promotions.

Principal of KHIT, Guntur district, B.S.B. Reddy said that rapid technological advancements and the convergence of different technologies were transforming the employment landscape. While certain job roles were becoming obsolete, new opportunities were emerging simultaneously. He expressed confidence that the seminar would help students gain clarity, build confidence and address uncertainties about their career choices.
Executive Director, KHIT, KHM Bharadwaj, Assistant Director, SRM-AP V.V.S. Pradeep and V. Amar from The Hindu were among those participated in the programme.

Addressing students at a seminar on ‘Career Opportunities in Management & Technology’, organised by The Hindu FIC and Paari School of Business, SRM AP, he urged them to explore opportunities beyond conventional career paths and make informed choices driven by their interests and determination.

Through real-life examples, anecdotes and interactive discussions, Prof. Satya highlighted how several successful professionals from engineering and science backgrounds had utilised their technical knowledge to emerge as prominent leaders in diverse fields.

He emphasised that passion, perseverance and a willingness to learn could open doors to limitless career opportunities.

Logo for The Hindu FIC & SRM AP seminar on careers in management and technology

He underlined the growing importance of analytical thinking, comprehension and proficiency in emerging technologies, particularly Artificial Intelligence (AI), in preparing students for future careers. Executive Director of Kallam Haranadhareddy Institute of Technology (KHIT) Navya Kallam said that the world offered opportunities across diverse sectors and that engineering graduates could explore areas beyond their core disciplines.

She pointed out that skills such as accounting, which is considered the backbone of any business, could help students become successful entrepreneurs.

KHIT Director Uma Shankar Reddy observed that there was no age limit for acquiring new skills.

Citing the example of the institution’s founder K. Haranadhareddy, who learnt music at the age of 75 and performed at temples, he encouraged students to remain open to learning throughout their lives. He also stressed that higher educational qualifications could strengthen career prospects, noting that additional qualifications often offered an advantage in career advancement and promotions.

articles.title: 12 of family injured in fire caused by CNG leak in M.P.'s Orchha; two of them critical
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Scrap dealer Khalil had purchased a CNG cylinder from someone and was trying to dismantle it to extract brass and other metals when the gas leaked out of it and sparked a fire

Twelve members of a family, including three children, suffered burn injuries in a fire that broke out following a CNG leak at a scrap shop in Madhya Pradesh's Orchha town on Friday (November 6, 2026), police said.

The injured were taken to a hospital in Jhansi in neighbouring Uttar Pradesh for treatment, and the condition of two of them — scrap dealer Khalil (60) and his son Sameer (30) — is stated to be critical, Orchha police station house officer Jitendra Singh Gurjar told PTI .
Mr. Khalil had purchased a CNG cylinder from someone and was trying to dismantle it to extract brass and other metals when the gas leaked out of it and sparked a fire, he said.
The blaze engulfed the premises, causing 12 members of Mr. Khalil's family to suffer burn injuries, he said.

Niwari Superintendent of Police Rai Singh Narwaria and District Collector Jamuna Bhide reached the spot after receiving information about the incident, and arranged for the injured to be shifted to the Jhansi medical hospital, the inspector said.
No case has been registered in connection with the incident so far, Mr. Gurjar said, adding that the police would take action based on the investigation.

articles.title: Delhi’s Mustafabad election official lodges police complaint seeking FIR over false Form 7s filing
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Delhi’s north east District Election Officer (DEO) Ajay Kumar told The Hindu that they have verified the news report independently and found 36 of the 37 Form 7s to be false/fabricated

The Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) of Mustafabad constituency has lodged a police complaint on Friday (November 7, 2026) seeking FIR under Section 31 of RP Act against the BLA following The Hindu’s report that false Form 7s have been filed seeking deletions of voters who are living at their addresses.

The north east District Election Officer (DEO ) Ajay Kumar told The Hindu that election officials have verified the news report independently and found 36 of the 37 Form 7s to be false/fabricated. “In connection with reports appearing in print and social media regarding false and fabricated Form-7, a police complaint has been lodged today by the ERO for registration of an FIR under Section 31 of the RP 1950 against the BLA,” a press release from his office also stated.

The Hindu reported on October 30 that in polling part area 129 of Mustafabad constituency, 28 Form 7s seeking deletions of electors found to be living in the area were filed by a BLA registered under Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), Chandra Shekhar Nainwal, as per Election Commission of India (ECI) records till October 28. While Mr. Nainwal denied filing these applications and any association with BJP, speaking to The Hindu , nine fresh applications were filed naming him as objector on October 29-30. The reasons cited in these applications were “absent/permanently shifted” and “dead”.

It further said that all 37 forms were scrutinised by the BLO/AERO who found that three electors who were claimed to be dead were found alive at their addresses. All others were also found living at their addresses, as reported by The Hindu .

“Only one case is found to be true whereas 36 cases are found to be false/fabricated. Since the BLA/Objector has knowingly made false statement or declaration in the Form-7, action under Section 31 of the RP act has been invoked for making false statement /declaration in writing in connection with preparation /revision of electoral roll,” the release mentioned.

It stated that verification and inquiry in respect of other Form-7 applications is in progress. As per The Hindu analysis, over 77% of the total 1,021 Form 7s received till November 3 names 20 BJP BLAs as objector. All are against Muslim electors, and several have been found residing at their addresses in different areas.
“Necessary action, as per the guidelines of the Election Commission of India and the extant Act, shall be taken,” the DEO stated in the press release.
Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls / Election Commission of India

articles.title: Agasthyamalai conservation case: SC directs temporary and non-resident silk cotton cultivators not eligible for protection under FRA Act
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court directed on Friday that individuals with temporary residence in the Agasthyamalai biosphere or those living entirely outside the forest boundaries cannot be classified as traditional forest dwellers merely for cultivating silk cotton within the forest.

“Persons falling in Category II and Category III, as classified in the additional affidavit of September 6 filed by Department of Revenue, State of Tamil Nadu, shall be excluded from consideration as forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers for the purposes of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 or FRA Act,” a Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta directed.

According to Tamil Nadu’s own affidavit, 232 persons are cultivating the forest area with temporary residence while 2,767 persons who occupy 2,867.70 hectares land are residing outside the forest boundary and are managing silk cotton cultivation.

The order was passed in furtherance of a May 2026 judgment, which had issued various directions for a structured and time-bound process of eviction, rehabilitation and ecological restoration in the forest areas. The court had ordered the preparation of a division-wise eviction plan, removal of encroachments, and action against identified government servants.

It had imposed a prohibition on approval or commencement of new non-forestry activities or diversion proposals within the Agasthyamalai landscape, and directed continued monitoring of the area by the Central Empowered Committee (CEC).

Justice Mehta, who authored the order, held the State government “primarily responsible” for delaying the receipt of claims under the 2006 Act. Noting that so far only around 40 gram sabhas had become functional to commence the process of inviting claims, the government gave a last opportunity of 30 days to the State government to complete the formation of the remaining gram sabhas. The process of adjudication of the claims would be concluded within a period of five months from the date of constitution of the gram sabhas.

The court further constituted a ‘special committee’ chaired by former Chief Justice of India B.R. Gavai to supervise the expeditious disposal of claims and scrutinise the orders passed by the competent authorities under the 2006 Act.

The Supreme Court directed the CEC to furnish an opinion regarding the government’s view that silk cotton was a ‘minor forest produce’. This is significant for the biosphere. Presently, 3,637.83.2 hectares of the 5,072.64.3 hectares of forest land is under silk cotton cultivation.

Giving a prima facie view against the State’s claim of historical cultivation of silk cotton, the court said “what emerges from the government affidavits is the promotion and sponsored cultivation of silk cotton as a commercial crop”.

“The concept of planned cultivation of commercial crops is totally contrary to the very concept of a naturally occurring minor forest produce. If commercial crops are permitted to be cultivated in the forest areas, the very nature of the forest is bound to change… The fact that large swathes of forest are being destroyed under the garb of cultivation of silk cotton,” the court observed.

Separately, the court directed the CEC to examine the National Highway Authority of India’s proposal relating to NH-744, including the proposed Puliara–Edamon tunnel section, which requires permission for diversion of a limited extent of reserved forest land in the biosphere.

articles.title: Did all the murders happen in the small house on the terrace?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Indushekhar lived with his wife Sunita and daughter in a small house, barely 500 sq. ft, on the terrace of a two-storey building, nestled among several commercial establishments, 50 metres from the famous Bhashyam Circle, Rajajinagar.

The building has commercial establishments on the ground floor, including a watch repair shop, a tea stall and a small condiments shop. The entire first floor was occupied by a small political party. Indushekar’s house is on the second floor, which also serves as the terrace.
Household appliances were crammed into the space, with several other household items scattered around. A board on the wall read, “Police Voice”.

Reaching the second floor itself through a very narrow staircase itself is a task. This has raised questions as to whether all seven murders were committed here in the house. However, the accused claimed that the murders took place inside his house. The location has raised several questions, as the building has very little space to move around.
However, the police investigation indicates a high probability that the murders took place there. “He may have cleaned the entire scene, but residues were found at the crime scene,” the officer said.

How did he transport the bodies down to the road into his car is a question that has left the police puzzled. He couldn’t have done it alone and that is where police suspect the role of the minor daughter. Given the lane mostly has commercial establishments, the police suspect that he could have shifted the bodies only during night time.

articles.title: Bamboo shelters, cool roofs to climate-proof Telangana cities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The State is drawing up a ₹20,000-crore project pipeline and a series of policy measures to prepare its cities for rising temperatures and erratic rainfall. The plan, which also includes waste reclamation, sewage treatment and digital monitoring of water supply, seeks to build climate resilience across urban local bodies

From bamboo bus shelters that offer shade and cooling to commuters, to the reclamation of waste dumps and the plugging of water supply leaks, Telangana is drawing up a broad plan to make its cities more resilient to climate change. The measures, backed by new urban policies and a project pipeline worth about ₹20,000 crore, are part of the State’s long-term Telangana Rising 2047 vision.

The roadmap seeks to integrate climate concerns into urban planning, infrastructure development and municipal services across urban local bodies (ULBs), said Municipal Administration and Urban Development secretary T.K. Sreedevi. The policy framework is being strengthened through a mandatory Urban Road Code, a Cool Roof Policy, a Heatwave Action Plan and a Treated Water Reuse Policy. Of the 43 projects proposed under the Urban Challenge Fund (UCF), three have secured approval.

Sreedevi said. The policy framework is being strengthened through a mandatory Urban Road Code, a Cool Roof Policy, a Heatwave Action Plan and a Treated Water Reuse Policy. Of the 43 projects proposed under the Urban Challenge Fund (UCF), three have secured approval.

Heatwaves and erratic rainfall are becoming increasingly evident across Telangana, though their impact varies by region. The government says this calls for location-specific interventions based on climate data. The challenge is significant: the State’s cities account for net emissions of about 66.56 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, with buildings, transport, wastewater, waste management and urban expansion among the major contributors.

Some interventions are already under way. Bamboo misting bus shelters in Khammam use a low-carbon building material while providing relief to commuters. Bio-mining of legacy waste dumps is aimed at reducing methane emissions and reclaiming land. The government is also working to reduce non-revenue water through leak detection, pipeline renewal and digital monitoring, besides expanding underground sewerage networks and reusing treated wastewater.
The bio-mining programme has helped avoid an estimated 5.6 lakh tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions and reclaimed about 418 acres for productive urban use, Ms. Sreedevi said.

To coordinate these efforts, a State Climate Centre for Cities has been established at the office of the Commissioner and Director of Municipal Administration. It will coordinate city-level climate action plans, maintain a climate data repository and provide technical support to municipalities.

Dedicated Climate Change Cells, city-specific action plans and nine Climate Action Officers are also planned for municipal corporations outside Hyderabad: Greater Warangal, Karimnagar, Khammam, Nizamabad, Ramagundam, Nalgonda, Mancherial, Mahabubnagar and Kothagudem.

The Telangana Urban Climate Atlas, a climate intelligence platform, has been set up to help municipalities identify vulnerable zones, prioritise investments and track climate indicators. Capacity-building programmes have been conducted for representatives of 113 ULBs to strengthen preparedness and project planning.

A key intervention is the Cool Roof Policy, effective from April 1, 2023, to March 31, 2028. It targets 300 sq km of cool roofs, including 200 sq km in the Hyderabad metropolitan region and 100 sq km in other urban local bodies. Cool roofs reflect about 80% of incoming sunlight, against 20% for conventional roofs. They can lower indoor temperatures by 2.1°C to 4.3°C and reduce air-conditioning costs by up to 20%. Full implementation is expected to save nearly 600 million units of electricity annually and generate a one-time carbon offset of about 30 million tonnes of carbon dioxide.

The policy covers government and commercial buildings and residential properties on plots of 600 square yards and above. Compliance has been integrated into the ‘Build Now’ building approval system and linked to occupancy certification. The government has also set a three-year target for retrofitting all non-residential buildings.

Urban heat mitigation proposals for Ramagundam and Adilabad are being prepared under UCF financing. Both cities are among the 29 ULBs covered by the World Bank-supported Telangana Urban Transformation and Jobs Programme, which includes urban greening, shaded public spaces and cool-roof measures.

articles.title: Karnataka CM ridicules BJP leaders for trying to take credit for PM’s visit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Friday alleged that some BJP leaders were trying to take credit for Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Bengaluru on November 13 to inaugurate the metro Pink Line, even though he was arriving on the official invitation of the State government.

Without taking the name of BJP MP Tejasvi Surya, the Chief Minister alleged that some BJP leaders were trying to take publicity by claiming that they were responsible for the Prime Minsiter’s proposed visit.
Speaking to media persons in Kanakapura, he wondered why the BJP leaders were tying to take publicity for this event though they had nothing to do with it.
“We are developing metro network by borrowing money. I will present some of these issues before the Prime Minister on November 13,” he said.

articles.title: Governor asks for status report on all public universities in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Sudha Yadav, Governor of Karnataka and Chancellor of universities in the State, directed all public universities in the State to conduct a comprehensive review of their current operations and identify areas requiring improvement. The Governor instructed all Vice-Chancellors to prepare and submit a detailed report on the same. “This report should cover the current status of their respective universities, key achievements, challenges, shortcomings, and specific measures proposed for improvement,” she stated.

Addressing the Vice-Chancellors of various universities and officials from the Karnataka State Higher Education Council at Lok Bhavan, the Governor emphasised the need to strengthen the quality, transparency, accountability and overall performance of universities across the State.

“Emphasis must be placed on the effective implementation of the National Education Policy and the State Education Policy, strong coordination between industries and universities, as well as skill development, research, innovation and employability,” she said.
The Governor called upon all Vice-Chancellors and the Karnataka State Higher Education Council to work in coordination and collaboration to strengthen the higher education system in Karnataka.

articles.title: Periyar Arivulagam books row: political leaders raise concern over allegations, call for action
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Kamal Haasan demands the immediate withdrawal of the fake books from all libraries. M.H. Jawahirullah wants the formation of an independent committee to examine all books procured for the public library. Others, including Anbumani Ramadoss and K. Annamalai, want the government to take up a thorough investigation of the allegations

After writer Perumal Murugan wrote about alleged irregularities in the procurement of books for Periyar Arivulagam, a newly inaugurated public library in Coimbatore, Makkal Needhi Maiam (MNM) founder and Rajya Sabha Member Kamal Haasan said on Friday that “there can be no greater disgrace to the Tamil language than this”.

He pointed out that books containing fabricated information could cause immense damage in the long run. In a statement, he said the reputation of Tamil language would be irreparably damaged if people read, took notes, and incorporated the contents of (fabricated books) into speeches, written works, and research.

“Whoever is responsible for this has betrayed the Tamil language. I urge the Government of Tamil Nadu to immediately withdraw these fake books from all libraries and have them dumped on the streets and burnt. The publishing houses responsible for this must be sealed. We owe a debt of gratitude to writer Mr. Murugan for exposing this fraud,” Mr. Haasan said.
Manithaneya Makkal Katchi president and MLA M.H. Jawahirullah said allegations raised by Mr. Murugan had caused considerable shock and concern.
Manithaneya Makkal Katchi president M.H. Jawahirullah. | Photo Credit: B. VELANKANNI RAJ

He said: “It has come to light that 1,800 books published under the name of a publishing house called Akalvilakku Publications have been procured and placed on the library’s fourth floor. This publishing house, which is unfamiliar to serious readers, has raised suspicions that it may have been established specifically to supply books to the library. Furthermore, Mr. Murugan has alleged that books were produced with the assistance of artificial intelligence, without the proper application of technical expertise; that the authors’ names are either pseudonyms or fictitious; that the International Standard Book Numbers (ISBNs) mentioned in the books cannot be found when checked online; and that the publisher’s address also appears to be unreliable,” he said.

Mr. Jawahirullah said, “An independent committee must be constituted to examine all books procured for the Periyar Arivulagam to date, including their publishers, authors, ISBNs, and pricing details, and a thorough inquiry must be conducted into the registration, addresses, owners, and activities of the suspicious publishing houses, including Agal Vilakku Publications.”

Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) president and Virudhunagar MP B. Manickam Tagore alleged: “Everyone knows that the DMK government was replete with enormous corruption. No scheme was devoid of corruption. If there has been this level of corruption in the procurement of books, it is scary to think how much corruption would have been there in the construction of the building. The Tamil Nadu government should order an investigation.”
TNCC president B. Manickam Tagore. | Photo Credit: B. JOTHI RAMALINGAM
He added that all the books kept in Periyar Arivulagam should be audited and fabricated books should be removed.

PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss urged the State government to investigate the allegations of corruption that have surfaced in the procurement of book for the public library, which was established by the DMK government.
PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss. | Photo Credit: S. SIVA SARAVANAN

fullParagraphs: On his social media site, Donald Trump praised Susie Wiles and said she’d continue working for his political organisation

President Donald Trump said Friday (November 6, 2026) that Stephen Miller was replacing Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff, mere days after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterm elections.
On his social media site, Mr. Trump praised Ms. Wiles and said she’d continue working for his political organisation. Ms. Wiles also released a social media statement on Friday (November 6, 2026).

"Serving President Trump in the White House has been the honour of a lifetime. Mr. Miller, long a key member of Mr. Trump’s inner circle, is a key architect of the administration’s hard-line immigration policies.

articles.title: West Bengal election is not legally valid: Former CEC S.Y. Quraishi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The former top poll official also reinstated that the Election Commission of India is supposed to make decisions based on a majority

Former Chief Election Commissioner S.Y. Quraishi alleged that the West Bengal elections were not legally valid. He reinstated that the decisions at the Election Commission of India should be based on a majority.

“Were the West Bengal elections legally valid? In my opinion, it was not. I have said this several times; I will say it again. Now it is in front of the Supreme Court; I am hoping they will take the right decision,” Mr. Quraishi said. He further added that some parts of it may have been valid but also said that in places where there was suspicious of majority Muslim voters being removed must be rechecked and go for re-polls if needed.

“This government has been in power for 6-7 months. People are happy. But some people are raising questions, maybe because they did not get the outcome that they desired,” Minister Dilip Ghosh said on Friday (November 6, 2026), reacting to Mr. Quraishi’s allegations. He also warned that accepting the people’s verdict and choice of government is the right decision; otherwise the people opposing it have a “tough” road ahead.

This comes after the former CEC raised allegations against the SIR process and discrepancies at the West Bengal elections while delivering the keynote address at the Hashim Abdul Halim Memorial Lecture on Thursday (November 5, 2026) in Kolkata.

“The CEC is not the Election Commission. The rules first call for unanimous decisions. If that is not possible, there must be a majority-based decision among the three members of the ECI,” Mr. Quraishi said. He added that the CEC is not the ECI on their own, and their decision alone cannot be final.

The former CEC said this in reference to The Indian Express report, which had claimed that election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised at least 14 objections to the various decisions allegedly taken unilaterally by CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

Meanwhile, Mr. Quraishi also said that the voter is not supposed to beg for their voting rights; rather, tradition in the past ensured that voter cards were delivered to the homes of each voter, and they did not have to negotiate to be included in the voter lists. He accused the special intensive revision (SIR) was used as a process to do backdoor checks for citizenships.

“It was neither smooth nor transparent. So many questions were raised that are currently being heard in the Supreme Court. Now, things will come out clearly once their judgment arrives, regarding what went wrong and what was correct,” Mr. Quraishi added.

articles.title: Pakistan says willing to issue visa to Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann for visit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: On October 23, Bhagwant Mann had said that he had been invited to attend the World Punjabi Conference in Lahore on November 27 questioning whether he would be allowed to travel to Pakistan
Pakistan on Friday (November 6, 2026) said it would consider issuing a visa to Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann if the Indian politician wished to visit the country.
Pakistan Foreign Office Spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan made the remarks during his weekly media briefing in response to a question about the possible visit of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader.

The Pakistani government would “consider issuing him a visa if he wished to visit the country”, Mr. Khan said, clarifying that whether the Indian government permits Mr. Mann to travel to Pakistan was an entirely separate matter.
On October 23, Mr. Mann had said that he had been invited to attend the World Punjabi Conference in Lahore on November 27.
However, he questioned whether he would be allowed to travel to Pakistan. “Our culture is the same. Many poets from here will go there,” he had said.
Mr. Mann had also expressed his desire that all legislators of the Punjab Legislative Assembly visit Kartarpur Sahib in Pakistan if the Kartarpur Corridor reopened.

The corridor, which connects Dera Baba Nanak in India's Punjab with the historic Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Kartarpur, Pakistan, was established to facilitate Sikh pilgrims travelling to the shrine associated with Guru Nanak Dev, the founder of Sikhism.
It allows Indian pilgrims to visit the gurdwara without requiring a visa for Pakistan, subject to the applicable arrangements.

The corridor has remained closed to pilgrim movement from the Indian side since May 7, 2025, when India launched pre-dawn missile strikes on nine terror targets in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir following the Pahalgam terror attack.
Pakistan said it remained ready to facilitate pilgrims once the restrictions were lifted.
The foreign office spokesperson said Pakistan welcomes pilgrims of all faiths and remains committed to facilitating visits to religious sites.

He said the country issued more than 9,000 visas to Indian religious pilgrims in 2025, including Sikh and Hindu pilgrims, and issued over 4,000 additional visas to Sikh pilgrims during the first half of this year.

articles.title: Supreme Court decision on BBMB arrears a victory for Himachal, says CM Sukhu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The order settles a decades-old dispute over Himachal Pradesh’s 7.19% share in the power generated from the projects

Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Friday (November 6, 2026) termed the Supreme Court’s decision directing Punjab and Haryana to supply 11,973 million units of electricity to the State over 20 years towards its outstanding dues from the Bhakra-Nangal and Beas hydroelectric projects a historic victory for its people.

The order settles a decades-old dispute over Himachal Pradesh’s 7.19% share in the power generated from the projects. The State will receive nearly 60 crore units annually during the lean season, generating an estimated revenue of ₹10,000 crore to ₹20,000 crore over the 20-year period, depending on electricity prices, Mr. Sukhu said in a statement.

He said the decision could fetch the State additional revenue of up to ₹1,000 crore annually. Even at ₹6 per unit, Himachal Pradesh would earn at least ₹500 crore a year, while a rate of ₹13-14 per unit would significantly increase the returns.

Mr. Sukhu attributed the outcome to the State government’s sustained legal battle and determination to secure its financial rights. He described it as the fourth major success in protecting Himachal Pradesh’s interests, citing earlier victories in matters relating to Wildflower Hall, the Kishau Dam among others.
The Chief Minister said the government was also pursuing its claims over the Shanan Power Project and the water cess.

The additional revenue, he said, would be used to strengthen education and healthcare, improve road infrastructure, generate employment and ensure timely payment of financial benefits to government employees.
Congratulating the State’s nearly 75 lakh residents, Mr. Sukhu said protecting its resources and making Himachal Pradesh self-reliant remained a top priority for his government.

articles.title: A missing persons complaint that unravelled Bengaluru’s seven murders
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Senior police officers said that Sunita, the accused’s wife, and Roopavathi, his mother-in-law, were the first to be murdered.

It was not until the mother of Nalini, one of the seven allegedly killed by cab driver-turned-YouTuber Indushekhar, lodged a missing person complaint that the police found the first clue to the murders. While the murders allegedly took place between October 16 and October 31, the last two bodies were disposed of on November 1 or 2.

Senior police officers said that Sunita, the accused’s wife, and Roopavathi, his mother-in-law, were the first to be murdered. Sunita and Indushekhar had been married for 20 years, and an officer said they had been having regular arguments throughout their marriage. Sunita worked as a typist for an advocate, while Indushekhar was a cab driver. Their respective jobs were often a point of contention between them.
“Indushekhar claimed that he was verbally abused and harassed by his wife and her family, while her brothers also encouraged her to fight with him,” a senior officer said.
Prima facie , the police have found that Indushekhar had been planning the murders for over a year. The growing friction and pent-up anger allegedly came to a head following a recent meeting.

“The accused claimed that Roopavathi had visited his house on October 14, when she and Sunita reportedly verbally abused him. This became a trigger point, and he wanted to eliminate them,” the officer said.

According to the police, Sunita and Roopavathi were murdered first. Subsequently, the accused invited Sunita’s younger brother Shivakumar and his wife Divya to his house on the pretext of hosting a dinner party. The couple were then killed along with their seven-year-old son Puneeth. On October 30, the accused allegedly invited Shankar, another brother of Sunita, and his wife Nalini, and allegedly murdered them.

On November 3, Tungamma, Nalini’s mother, approached the police, stating that her daughter’s phone was switched off and that their house in Srirampura was also locked. Tungamma subsequently went to Indushekar’s house to check on him but found that his house was locked as well.

Sensing that something was amiss, she contacted Divya’s mother Kalavathi, who also said that her daughter and son-in-law were missing. Tungamma then lodged a missing person complaint with the Srirampura police.

articles.title: Epic failures: on electoral roll, welfare
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The electoral roll cannot be used to determine welfare beneficiaries

Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

Not every citizen is an eligible voter, and tying benefits to the electoral roll is illogical and also cruel. In West Bengal, lakhs were deleted from the rolls , many for dubious “logical discrepancies”. In the appeals heard for reinstatement, 93% resulted in the restoration of names by September 2026, pointing to massive pre-election disenfranchisement. The Court has stated that it is yet to adjudicate on the legality of the ECI’s “logical discrepancies” method. The SIR was designed by the ECI to restrict enrolment through stringent residency criteria; thus, itinerant voters had to prove their eligibility. The Opposition, civil society and even some of the BJP’s allies have objected to this, but the BJP refuses to acknowledge the SIR’s flaws. This is partly because it has benefited from disenfranchisement — as in West Bengal. But the Minister’s remarks suggest another reason. The BJP-led coalition sees the pruned electoral rolls as a way to limit welfare, especially at a time when growth in tax revenues has slowed because of the Centre’s policies. Inordinately delaying the Census, changing the procedure to appoint Election Commissioners, who then run an exercise that disenfranchises millions by design, and now, using the resultant rolls to decide who gets welfare, all cut at the heart of the painstakingly built constitutional welfare state. The sooner the Court decides the petitions against the SIR, and reiterates that its rolls cannot be used to curtail welfare, the better.

articles.title: Assam OIL facility fire death toll rises to two
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Five other workers injured in the incident are undergoing treatment

The death toll in the explosion at an Oil India Limited (OIL) facility in eastern Assam’s Dibrugarh rose to two after one of six persons injured in Friday’s (November 6, 2026) fire died at a private hospital on Saturday (November 7, 2026) morning.
Reportedly working for a Mumbai-based private agency engaged by the oil exploration major, 40-year-old Tapas Gogoi died at around 3 a.m., taking the death toll in the fire incident to two.
The other person, identified as Raju Dutta, died from the impact of the explosion on Friday (November 6, 2026) morning.
The fire broke out at around 9.05 a.m. at the indirect bath heater in OIL’s intermediate tank farm at Tengakhat. The bath heater was isolated on November 4 for maintenance.
Five other workers injured in the incident are undergoing treatment.
According to OIL, fire and emergency services personnel rushed to the facility and launched fire-fighting operations to extinguish the fire by 12.30 p.m. on Friday (November 6, 2026).

Officials said OIL constituted an internal inquiry committee to investigate the incident, identify its immediate and underlying causes, assess damage and suggest proactive measures to prevent such incidents in future.

articles.title: Bus overturns as driver falls asleep, seven injured in Tirupati
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The driver has reportedly dozed off and applied sudden brake while the bus slipped towards an adjacent canal, which was not clear due to stagnant rainwater on the road

At least seven passengers were injured after a private bus met with an accident on the National Highway (NH-140) near Ithepalle village in Chandragiri mandal of Tirupati district on the early hours of Saturday (November 7, 2026).

According to the police, the bus belonging to Sri Naveen Travels was proceeding from Bengaluru in neighbouring Karnataka to Bhubaneshwar in Odisha, when it overturned opposite a Bharat Petroleum bunk around 4.30 am.

As per the preliminary information, the driver has reportedly dozed off and applied sudden brake while the bus slipped towards an adjacent canal, which was not clear due to stagnant rainwater on the road.

The injured passengers, including the driver, were admitted into Sri Venkateswara Institute of Medical Sciences (SVIMS) Hospital in Tirupati. The remaining 34 passengers were sent to their destinations in another bus.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu govt sanctions ₹198 crore as honorarium for officials involved in 2026 Assembly election
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A Government order, issued by the Public (Elections) Department, stated one month’s basic pay, subject to a maximum of ₹45,000, whichever is less, will be paid to officials and staff members involved in 2026 Assembly election

The Tamil Nadu Government has accorded sanction for the release of ₹198 crore towards payment of honorarium to officials and staff members who worked for the conduct of the 2026 Assembly election across all 234 Assembly constituencies in the State.

A Government Order to this effect was issued by the Public (Elections) Department. Accordingly, one month’s basic pay, subject to a maximum of ₹45,000, whichever is less, will be paid to District Election Officers (DEOs), Returning Officers and Assistant Returning Officers of Assembly constituencies, District Revenue Officers (Elections), Personal Assistants (Elections) to Collectors, Special Tahsildars, Commissioners of Corporations, District Revenue Officers (DROs), Deputy Tahsildars (Elections), Zonal Officers and Liaison Officers for Observers.

Similarly, one month’s basic pay, subject to a maximum of ₹30,000, whichever is less, will be paid to officers and staff working in the election wings of the offices of DEOs, DROs, Tahsildars, Commissioners of Corporations and Municipalities. The same arrangement will apply to members of Flying Squads, Video Surveillance Teams, Video Viewing Teams, Accounting Teams, Model Code of Conduct Teams, Assistant Expenditure Observers, Static Surveillance Teams and Zonal Assistants.
Other categories of staff have also been sanctioned honorarium under various slabs. This honorarium would be paid to the officers and staff members through DEOs concerned, the order said.

A Government order, issued by the Public (Elections) Department, stated one month’s basic pay, subject to a maximum of ₹45,000, whichever is less, will be paid to officials and staff members involved in 2026 Assembly election

The Tamil Nadu Government has accorded sanction for the release of ₹198 crore towards payment of honorarium to officials and staff members who worked for the conduct of the 2026 Assembly election across all 234 Assembly constituencies in the State.

A Government Order to this effect was issued by the Public (Elections) Department. Accordingly, one month’s basic pay, subject to a maximum of ₹45,000, whichever is less, will be paid to District Election Officers (DEOs), Returning Officers and Assistant Returning Officers of Assembly constituencies, District Revenue Officers (Elections), Personal Assistants (Elections) to Collectors, Special Tahsildars, Commissioners of Corporations, District Revenue Officers (DROs), Deputy Tahsildars (Elections), Zonal Officers and Liaison Officers for Observers.

Similarly, one month’s basic pay, subject to a maximum of ₹30,000, whichever is less, will be paid to officers and staff working in the election wings of the offices of DEOs, DROs, Tahsildars, Commissioners of Corporations and Municipalities. The same arrangement will apply to members of Flying Squads, Video Surveillance Teams, Video Viewing Teams, Accounting Teams, Model Code of Conduct Teams, Assistant Expenditure Observers, Static Surveillance Teams and Zonal Assistants.

Other categories of staff have also been sanctioned honorarium under various slabs. This honorarium would be paid to the officers and staff members through DEOs concerned, the order said.

articles.title: CM Vijay orders ₹2,000-crore allocation to implement Vetri Laptop Scheme for college students
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Under the scheme, students pursuing first- and second-year undergraduate and diploma courses in government and government-aided colleges during the 2026-2027 academic year will be eligible for laptops

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Saturday (November 7, 2026) ordered the sanctioning of ₹2,000 crore to implement the Vetri Laptop Scheme with the objective to enhance the technological skills of college students.
According to an official release, the administrative sanction has been accorded by the State government to implement the scheme, which was announced in the Budget 2026-27, at a cost of ₹ 2,000 crore.

A High-Level Steering Committee, headed by the Chief Minister, will be constituted to monitor the implementation of the scheme. The Electronics Corporation of Tamil Nadu (ELCOT) has been granted administrative sanction to procure laptops and ensure quality control.

Under the scheme, students pursuing first- and second-year undergraduate and diploma courses in government and government-aided colleges during the 2026-2027 academic year will be eligible for laptops. The beneficiaries include students pursuing arts and science, engineering, polytechnic, ITI, medicine, veterinary sciences, fisheries, agriculture and law courses.

In addition, third- and fourth-year students pursuing professional courses in government and government-aided colleges who did not benefit from the laptop scheme during the 2025-26 academic year will also be covered. Considering the technological requirements of engineering students, they will be provided with laptops equipped with Intel Core i5 processors or equivalent specifications, the release added.

articles.title: Ex-Keralam Excise Commissioner flags corruption, bribery in report to govt; CPI(M) alleges Minister’s involvement
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In report submitted to State government shortly before being relieved from the post, Seeram Sambasiva Rao mentions that Excise Minister M. Liju was acquainted with one of the bar owners allegedly involved in the transactions

Former Keralam Excise Commissioner Seeram Sambasiva Rao, shortly before being relieved from the post , had submitted a report to the State government alleging corruption and collection of bribes by two senior officials of the Excise Department, officials said on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

Mr. Rao, who was serving as Excise Commissioner and Special Secretary in the Electronics and Information Technology Department, was transferred and posted as Special Secretary in the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Development Department.
In the report submitted to the government on Friday, Mr. Rao also mentioned that Excise Minister M. Liju was acquainted with one of the bar owners allegedly involved in the transactions.

According to the report, S. Vinod, who served as Joint Excise Commissioner (JEC), allegedly maintained close links with the owner of a bar in Muvattupuzha and acted as a liaison for the establishment in matters related to its licence.

An informant had alleged that Mr. Vinod demanded a monthly payment of ₹30,000 from the bar owner and had also received ₹50,000 for securing approvals related to bar timings and licence extensions, the report claimed.
The report also flagged allegations against Alappuzha Deputy Commissioner Ajay.
According to the information received by Mr. Rao, the owner of a bar at Kattachira in Kayamkulam was allegedly asked to pay ₹30,000 during the deputy commissioner’s inspection visits, it said.
The report identified the bar owner as Ratheesh and stated that he was known to the Excise Minister.
It also mentioned an alleged payment of ₹20,000 after Onam this year in connection with the renewal of the bar’s licence in April.
Mr. Rao recommended that Mr. Vinod and Mr. Ajay be immediately removed from field postings and transferred to offices such as the Excise Crime Records Bureau or Toddy Board.

He also recommended a Vigilance inquiry into the allegations of bribe collection, monthly payments and disproportionate assets against the two officials under relevant provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act.

The report further called for stricter controls on posting officials facing allegations of financial irregularities to sensitive locations and establishments, and recommended that future transfers and appointments at the JEC, Additional Excise Commissioner and Deputy Commissioner levels be considered based on reports from the Excise Commissioner.

articles.title: OMCs refute Karnataka’s E20 report, seeks additional details about procedure
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The state-owned OMCs held the 56 samples tested by them from across the state reported an average 19.3% ethanol content in the vehicular fuel.

Refuting observations about ethanol blend in petrol being as high as 31% in Karnataka, the three state-owned oil-marketing companies (OMCs) stated the tests were not conducted in accordance with prescribed statutory and technical procedure.

Citing discrepancies with findings from their own quality monitoring, they urged the State government to share the complete counterpart sampling documentation, outlet-wise laboratory reports, and details about the adopted testing methodology, and samples for retesting.

“The OMCs remain committed to cooperating with the state government and other competent authorities in conducting joint sampling and testing in accordance with the Control Order and the Marketing Discipline Guidelines, 2024,” it stated, adding, “Any deviation established through the prescribed procedure will be dealt with in accordance with applicable guidelines.”
The OMCs raised concerns about the Karnataka Dept of Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology’s use of the gas chromatography for evaluating ethanol concentration.
The process broadly entails separating compounds via vaporisation.

According to the OMCs, the certificates cited for the State government’s observations do not specify the applicable standard test method, the procedure for diluting the compounds or the reference material used for correction after vaporisation.
“In the absence of these essential details, the reported ethanol figures of 26-31% cannot be independently validated against the methodology prescribed under IS 17021,” the statement read.

Further, pointing to the Karnataka government’s reported observations, it observed, “Given that ethanol has a higher density than petrol, a higher ethanol proportion would ordinarily be expected to increase the density of the blend. This discrepancy [in Karnataka’s reported samples] further underscores the need for testing through the prescribed methodology and verification against appropriate reference samples.”
The three OMCs put forth that 56 samples from across the State tested by them conformed to the prescribed specifications, reporting ethanol content between at an average 19.3%.
Thus, arguing that the “substantially higher ethanol levels” reported by the State Dept. warrant a “transparent, technically sound and jointly verifiable testing exercise.”

On similar lines, putting forth concerns about the Karnataka State Dept’s observations on 10% mileage loss and the ensuing ₹62,000 crore loss to consumers, it called for a transparent assessment of actual vehicle performance data, material compatibility studies and documented repair costs.

articles.title: Amid price rise, Centre mandates rice, paddy stock declaration
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: To prevent hoarding, Union government allows five southern States to impose stock limits

With rice prices rising due to a deficient and uneven monsoon, the Centre on Friday (November 7, 2026) directed traders, retailers, wholesalers, processors and millers across the country to declare their rice and paddy stocks and allowed five southern States to impose stock limits to prevent hoarding.

Under a November 6 order, all traders and wholesalers, retailers, large retail chains and processors and millers in all States and Union Territories must declare stocks under six categories — Basmati rice, non-Basmati premium rice, non-Basmati rice, parboiled rice, broken rice and paddy.
Every unit holding stocks will have to update details on the Food Stock Portal (foodstock.dfpd.gov.in) every Friday, the Food Ministry said in a statement.
Units that are not registered on the portal or that violate stock limits will face action under Sections 6 and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.

In a separate letter, also dated November 6, the Centre has given its consent to Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana to impose stock limits on paddy and rice through control orders.

The limits will remain in force till January 31, 2027. The Centre and States will monitor implementation to ensure adequate availability and prevent hoarding and black marketing, an official statement said.

To improve availability, the Centre is allocating additional rice stocks to NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar for sale as Bharat Rice, and has asked them to explore all possible distribution channels, especially in the southern States.

The Centre has also doubled the target for rice sales through e-auction under the Open Market Sale Scheme (Domestic) for 2026-27 from 25 lakh tonnes to 50 lakh tonnes. Around 25 lakh tonnes had been sold to private parties by October 31, compared to 11 lakh tonnes in the same period of the last year.
Trade and industry experts said deficient and uneven rainfall had contributed to rice inflation, particularly in premium non-Basmati varieties, and pushed up paddy prices in several markets.
Retail rice inflation rose to 8.25% year-on-year in September from 5.89% in August, with the average retail price at around ₹48.23 per kg, about 12% higher than a year earlier.
Experts, however, said the situation was not a nationwide crisis.
With government rice stocks at comfortable levels, they said, pressure was sharpest in regions and grades where supplies were tight.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics

Top officials from Washington and Beijing held "frank" talks on their countries' testy trade relationship on Friday (November 6, 2026), ahead of an Asia-Pacific summit in China this month where their leaders are due to meet.
