articles.title: T.N. CM Vijay writes to PM Modi expressing concerns over inspection of Union govt. officials regarding Mekedatu dam project
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: CM Vijay said there was an apprehension growing among farmers of Tamil Nadu over the recent developments with respect to the proposed Mekedatu Dam Project of Karnataka

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Saturday (November 7, 2026) wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressing his concerns regarding the site inspection conducted by the Union government officials in connection with the Karnataka government’s proposal to construct the Mekedatu dam.

He urged the Prime Minister that no statutory or administrative approvals be granted without the consent of the co-basin States, while emphasising the need to ensure the sustained water availability in the Cauvery basin of Tamil Nadu.
In his letter, Mr. Vijay said there was an apprehension growing among farmers of Tamil Nadu over the recent developments with respect to the proposed Mekedatu Dam Project of Karnataka.

“The said proposal of Government of Karnataka to construct Mekedatu reservoir across Cauvery with a huge capacity of 67.16 TMC, just upstream of inter-State border between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, would not only prevent the flows due to Tamil Nadu but also prejudicially affect the monthly deliveries to the inhabitants of Cauvery Basin of Tamil Nadu, as stipulated by the Hon’ble Supreme Court,” Mr. Vijay said in his letter.

There have been frequent news reports on Karnataka Chief Minister’s meeting with the officials of Ministry of Jal Shakti (MoJS), Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change for clearance of DPR of Mekedatu Project, without the concurrence of Tamil Nadu, which keep the farmers of the State in a state of perpetual anxiety , he said.

“Earlier, a team of officers of the Government of India reportedly visited the proposed Mekedatu Dam site, as per the statements emanating from the State of Karnataka. The anxious farmers of Tamil Nadu view the site visit as an indication of tacit movement on a project that would jeopardise their very livelihood. Such actions, the purported site inspection by Government of India officials, have deepened the worries of the farmers of Cauvery delta, who are already struggling in this deficit water year (2026–27), due to Karnataka’s denial to ensure Tamil Nadu’s due share even on a pro-rata basis,” Mr. Vijay said.

Mr. Vijay also referred to his earlier letter dated July 28, where in he requested the Prime Minister to ensure that no statutory or administrative approval be granted to the Mekedatu Project, unless it is demonstrably consistent with the Final Award of the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal (CWDT) and the Hon’ble Supreme Court’s Judgment.

The Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly passed a unanimous Resolution on June 19, reiterating its demand on the proposed Mekedatu project and also filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court with a prayer to withdraw the guidelines issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti in December, 2025, on the preparation of DPR for irrigation and multi-purpose project proposals, exclusively for Cauvery basin, since the basin is held to be a deficit by the Tribunal in February, 2007. This matter is still pending in the Supreme Court of India, Mr. Vijay pointed out.

“It is vital that the rights of lower riparian States regarding both the quantum and regulated pattern of monthly releases remain fully protected and hence, consideration or examination of DPR of Mekedatu Project submitted by Karnataka or any unilateral technical evaluations or site inspections by central agencies at this juncture are highly inappropriate,” he said.

articles.title: A total of 28 illegal immigrants apprehended, expelled: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a post on X, Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma said the State government would continue its drive against infiltration and would not compromise on Assam's security and identity

“Police in Assam 's Sribhumi district apprehended and expelled 28 Bangladeshi nationals allegedly staying illegally in the State,” Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said on Saturday (November 7, 2026).
In a post on X, Mr. Sarma said the State government would continue its drive against infiltration and would not compromise on Assam's security and identity.

"Assam's patience with infiltration is over. Twenty-eight illegal migrants detected by Sribhumi Police were expelled. We will continue this mission with unwavering determination. No compromise on our borders. No compromise on the security and identity of Assam,'' he added.

Assam has an integrated checkpost in Sribhumi and a land customs station at Mankachar. Mr. Sarma had earlier said the State government is committed to an infiltration-free Assam. The Border Security Force has intensified its vigil along the 1,885 km Indo-Bangladesh border in the Northeast since the 2024 disturbances in Bangladesh. Assam Police has also maintained a high alert along the International Border to prevent illegal entry.

🏛️ National & Polity 📅 07 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

A total of 28 illegal immigrants apprehended, expelled: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

In a post on X, Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma said the State government would continue its drive against infiltration and would not compromise on Assam's security and identity

“Police in Assam 's Sribhumi district apprehended and expelled 28 Bangladeshi nationals allegedly staying illegally in the State,” Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

In a post on X, Mr. Sarma said the State government would continue its drive against infiltration and would not compromise on Assam's security and identity.

"Assam's patience with infiltration is over. Twenty-eight illegal migrants detected by Sribhumi Police were expelled. We will continue this mission with unwavering determination. No compromise on our borders. No compromise on the security and identity of Assam,'' he added.

Assam has an integrated checkpost in Sribhumi and a land customs station at Mankachar. Mr. Sarma had earlier said the State government is committed to an infiltration-free Assam. The Border Security Force has intensified its vigil along the 1,885 km Indo-Bangladesh border in the Northeast since the 2024 disturbances in Bangladesh. Assam Police has also maintained a high alert along the International Border to prevent illegal entry.

articles.title: Karnataka Police Complaints Authority member proposes seniority badges for police personnel
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: If implemented, Karnataka could become the first State in the country to introduce a structured system of seniority-based designations and uniform insignia for police personnel

A member of the Karnataka State Police Complaints Authority, has urged the State Government to introduce special designations and insignia on police uniforms to recognise the seniority of personnel based on their years of service, irrespective of promotions.

In a letter dated November 5 to Minister for Home, IT-BT and E-Governance Priyank Kharge, Karnataka State Police Complaints’ Authority member Mohan Kumar Danappa proposed introducing three categories of seniority for police personnel, from constables to non-IPS officers.

According to his proposal, personnel completing five years of service should be designated as ‘Senior’, those completing 10 years as ‘Super Senior’, and those completing 15 years as ‘Most Senior’. He has suggested that distinct insignia corresponding to these designations be displayed on the right side of the chest, above the nameplate.

Mr. Danappa pointed out that although police personnel generally become eligible for promotion after five years of service, promotions are largely dependent on the availability of vacancies. As a result, many experienced personnel continue in the same rank for years without any formal recognition of their seniority and experience.
He said the proposed system would recognise their long service, enhance their sense of responsibility and ensure that experienced personnel receive due respect within the department and society.

Citing the practice of providing black collar patches to IPS officers after 10 years of service, he said similar arrangements were also followed in certain State police forces and Central Armed Police Forces.

He also referred to the State Government’s recent initiatives to replace British-era police caps and introduce lanyards in place of whistle chains, stating that recognising seniority through uniform insignia would be another significant reform to boost the morale of police personnel.
If implemented, Karnataka could become the first State in the country to introduce a structured system of seniority-based designations and uniform insignia for police personnel, he said.
Mr. Danappa has requested the Home Minister to examine the proposal and issue necessary directions to the concerned authorities for its implementation.

articles.title: Bengaluru cab driver kills wife, six members of her family
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The murders are believed to have been carried out between October 16 and November 3, with the bodies dumped at multiple locations on Bengaluru’s outskirts, including one near the foothills of Nandi Hills in Chickballapur.

In a shocking murder spree in Bengaluru , a 52-year-old man allegedly killed his wife and six members of her family, including a seven-year-old boy, and disposed of the bodies over a span of 18 days, police sources said. An 11-year-old boy, who is also a relative of the accused, has been rescued.

The accused was allegedly assisted by his 17-year-old college-going daughter, whose exact role is yet to be established. Family disputes are believed to have been the motive for the murders, although the police have not ruled out any other angle and are interrogating the accused.

The prime accused, identified as Indushekar, a cab driver and YouTuber who also ran a monthly tabloid, has been arrested by the Rajajinagar police. The murders are believed to have been committed between October 16 and 31, while the last two bodies were reportedly disposed of on November 1 and 2.

A preliminary police investigation revealed that the accused, with the help of his daughter, invited the relatives to his house on the pretext of a non-vegetarian dinner or a party. “After dinner, when the relatives fell asleep, the accused used a grinding stone to kill the victims. There is also a suspicion that he may have spiked their food. However, the police are awaiting medical reports to ascertain the cause of death,” a source said.

According to the FIR, which also records the accused’s statements, the bodies were dumped at multiple locations on the city’s outskirts and elsewhere in the State, including Yercaud Ghat, Chamundi Hills, Nandi Hills, and Shiradi Ghat. He allegedly used his sedan car, that he used as a cab, to dispose of the bodies. So far, the police have been able to trace only one body, that of the seven-year-old boy.

The incident came to light after a family member of one of the deceased lodged a missing complaint at the Srirampura police station. Subsequent investigations led to Indushekar being detained, and his statements unravelled a series of horrific murders that allegedly took place at his house near Bhashyam Circle in Rajajinagar, north Bengaluru.

The deceased have been identified as Indushekar’s wife, Sunita (40); his mother-in-law, Roopavathi (65); his two brothers-in-law, Shivakumar (30) and Shankar (44); their wives, Divya (30) and Nalini (29); and Shivakumar’s son, Puneeth (7).

An investigator in the case told The Hindu that the accused had maintained that his wife and mother-in-law did not respect him and frequently verbally abused him, while her family supported them. “The accused claims to have been planning the murders for many months. A recent visit by his mother-in-law did not go well, which angered him,” the source told The Hindu.

articles.title: Siang dam protesters released in Arunachal Pradesh after nearly a month in detention
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The four, identified as Adum Tayom, Omak Paron, Okut Paloh and Oson Paron, were detained on October 9 under the Arunachal Pradesh Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 2014

Four protesters detained over the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh were released from Jully Central Jail near Itanagar on Saturday (November 7, 2026), nearly a month after their arrest, officials said.
The four, identified as Adum Tayom, Omak Paron, Okut Paloh and Oson Paron, were detained on October 9 under the Arunachal Pradesh Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 2014, they added.

Their release came a day after the State Government agreed to free them as a goodwill gesture while responding to demands raised by the Siang Indigenous Farmers' Forum (SIFF), which has been leading the protest against the proposed mega dam.
The development marks a significant step towards easing tensions in the Siang Valley, where opposition to the project has triggered protests and confrontations in recent months.

In a letter dated November 6, the Chief Minister's Office (CMO) also approved the reinstatement of suspended gaonburas and gaonburis affected by disciplinary action in connection with the SUMP agitation.
The Government, however, maintained that the withdrawal of FIRs against protesters would have to follow due legal process.

It also said the demand for withdrawal of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) and Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel from the region would be discussed during the proposed meeting with SIFF representatives, taking into account the prevailing security situation.
The Government has urged SIFF to resume dialogue and communicate a convenient date, along with a list of delegates, for a proposed meeting with Chief Minister Pema Khandu.
It also appealed to the organisation to encourage residents of Siang and Upper Siang districts to maintain peace and refrain from violence, intimidation and attacks.

The CMO's communication, signed by Shibu Thomas, Principal Private Secretary to the Chief Minister, reiterated the government's commitment to addressing the concerns of the Adi community through a mutually acceptable roadmap.
The release of the four protesters was among SIFF's key demands before agreeing to participate in talks with the government.
The forum had earlier rejected Mr. Khandu's invitation for dialogue, insisting that its demands, including the release of detainees and withdrawal of security forces, be addressed first.

articles.title: Agents booked, five fertility centres named in Hyderabad’s illegal oocyte racket; Telangana Women’s Commission questions inaction
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: While cases have been registered against a few agents in connection with the alleged illegal collection of eggs (oocytes) from economically vulnerable women, the Telangana Women’s Commission has questioned why no legal action has been initiated against the hospitals and fertility centres allegedly involved in the racket.

The alleged exploitation came to light after 43 women were rescued during simultaneous raids in Hyderabad. Women from economically weaker sections were allegedly offered between ₹20,000 and ₹30,000 for an egg donation cycle, while those operating the racket reportedly made an average of about ₹3 lakh from each cycle.

Expressing strong displeasure over the delay, the Commission said that despite its directions to the concerned authorities to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the hospitals and laboratories allegedly involved, no concrete steps had been taken against the institutions so far.

During her interaction with the affected women, Commission Chairperson Nerella Sharada said that she was informed about the alleged involvement of five institutions which include, Indira IVF Centre, Narmada Fertility Centre, Oasis Fertility Centre, Sadguru ART Centre and Padmaja Fertility Centre. The women also named an individual identified as Dr. Hussain in their complaints.
Ms. Nerella expressed concern over the fact that the whereabouts of Dr. Hussain remain unknown and that no case has been registered against him so far.

Questioning the delay in action, the Commission has urged senior officials of the health department to immediately conduct an inquiry into the allegations against the hospitals and IVF centres named by the affected women and initiate stringent legal action against those found responsible.

The Commission further warned that there would be serious consequences if there was any further delay in registering cases against those involved in unlawful activities concerning women’s bodily autonomy, dignity and health.

articles.title: Authoritarian leaders facing setbacks, says M.K. Muneer
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chairperson of the Kerala Administrative Reforms Commission M.K. Muneer urges the public to oppose hate speech irrespective of who makes it, asserting that there should be no compromise with those who spread hatred.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi is destined to meet the fate of Adolf Hitler and Benito Mussolini, M.K. Muneer, chairperson of the Kerala Administrative Reforms Commission, has said. He was inaugurating the delegates’ meet organised as part of the Keralam State conference of the Muslim Youth League here on Saturday (November 7).

Mr. Muneer said the people are living in an era when authoritarian leaders are facing setbacks. “That is why Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu are being forced to confront resistance. They will ultimately meet the same fate as Hitler and Mussolini. Narendra Modi, too, faces a similar future,” he was quoted as saying in a release.
He urged the public to oppose hate speech irrespective of who makes it, asserting that there should be no compromise with those who spread hatred.

Shweta Bhatt, wife of former IPS officer Sanjiv Bhatt, who was the chief guest at the delegates’ meet, said that the legal battle and imprisonment of her husband have entered its eighth year, but the family will not retreat from its struggle for truth and justice.
She said that asking questions and defending constitutional rights were the true expressions of patriotism.
Muslim Youth League State president Panakkad Syed Munavvar Ali Shihab Thangal presided over the meeting. State general secretary P.K. Firos delivered the welcome address, said the release.

Palem, four in Nizampatnam, three in Bapatla, two each in Amruthalur and Tsundur, and one each in Chirala, Karlapalem, Kolluru and Vemuru.
The JSP won three seats in Repalle, two each in Cherukupalli and Karlapalem, and one each in Chinaganjam and the remaining mandal as reflected in the district tally, taking its total to eight.
The YSRCP secured 19 seats, including four in P.V. Palem, three in Parchur, two each in Bapatla, Chinaganjam, Karlapalem and Martur, and one each in Chirala, Karamchedu, Kolluru and Tsundur.
In the ZPTC elections, the TDP won two seats and was leading in four more. It emerged victorious in P.V. Palem and Yeddanapudi, while it was ahead in Bhattiprolu, Cherukupalli, Nagaram and Parchur.

articles.title: No respite from deluge even a week after rain: Residents of Palakol complain
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Several colonies are in knee-deep water for the last few days, and there is no proper power supply and no supply of milk, vegetables and other essentials in some of the water logged areas, says the victims

With water still not receding even a week after Cyclone Murasu flooded the streets of Palakol in West Godavari district, residents see no help in sight as they complain that their efforts to raise the issue with authorities have gone in vain.

“The A.P. Housing Board Colony, Allu Venkata Satnarsyana Colony and the neighbouring areas were inundated. Flood entered many houses and damaged household articles,” said residents of Housing Board Colony.
As colonies were flooded, there has been no proper power supply, and streets remained inaccessible for milk and vegetable vendors, residents complained.
In some lanes, slush and garbage entered into the houses. Floodwater in the colonies has not receded, and snakes and poisonous reptiles were creating panic, said a resident, Vijaya Lakshmi.

“We have sent messages through social media groups to the Palakol Municipal and Revenue officials, and tried in vain to meet the public representatives. There has been no response from them,” said Sathi Babu of AVS Colony.

“Medicines and essentials are exhausted in several houses, and senior citizens, pregnant and lactating women were suffering, as the colonies are in knee-deep water,” Kumari, a resident whose house was damaged due to the cyclone, told The Hindu on Saturday.
A few people vacated as their houses were in floodwaters and went to safer places. There were no street lights too, Ms. Kumari added.

“When we visited the Sachivalayams, Revenue and Municipal offices, attenders and watchmen said the officers were on election duties. No steps have been taken to drain out the floodwater, a Kirana shop owner said.
“Flood water stagnated in low-lying areas, and many areas were water-logged for the last few days. We are trying to solve the problem,” an officer said.

articles.title: Curtain goes up on 10-day Kalpathy car festival
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The 10-day annual Kalpathy car festival began on Saturday with traditional rituals marking the start of one of Keralam’s well-known temple festivals. The ceremonial hoisting of flags (Dwajarohanam) at the four participating temples will take place on Sunday morning.

The festival is jointly organised by four temples in the Kalpathy heritage village: Visalakshi Sametha Viswanatha Swami Temple, Kalpathy; Manthakkara Mahaganapathy Temple, New Kalpathy; Lakshmi Narayan Perumal Temple, Old Kalpathy; and Prasanna Mahaganapathy Temple, Chathapuram. The festival will conclude on November 17.
With large crowds expected, the district police, government departments, Palakkad municipality and temple committees have coordinated security, traffic and other arrangements.

The temple committees have sought crowd management measures, police deployment and safety arrangements along the chariot routes and riverbanks. They have also called for restrictions on roadside vending and parking to keep the routes and approach roads clear.

The committees have proposed using open grounds, including the Government Victoria College ground, for vehicle parking and operating KSRTC mini-buses as shuttle services between the parking areas and the festival venue.

District police chief Abdul Rashi said the police would ensure security and work with the government departments, municipality and temple committees to manage the festival. The municipality has also assured support.
Ramesh Pisharody, MLA, said he would get the consent of the Ministers concerned to get Victoria College grounds for parking and KSRTC shuttle services to the venue.

articles.title: Indian diplomat elected to UN committee on administration, budgets
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Shivani Gupta will begin her three-year term in January 2027

articles.title: Airstrike kills 22 people near Yemen's capital, Houthi official says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Footage from Houthi-run Al-Masirah TV of the aftermath of November 7 strikes showed staff carrying limp bodies of young children out of ambulances, bringing the casualties to a local hospital

Airstrikes hit homes in a village near Yemen's capital, Sanaa, on Saturday (November 7, 2026), killing at least 22 people and wounding 30 others, mostly women and children, a spokesman for Yemen's Houthi-run Health Ministry said.

Speaking to The Associated Press , Anees Alasbahi accused Saudi Arabia of carrying out the strikes on al-Shariya. The AP could not independently verify the claims, and Saudi Arabia's Information Ministry did not immediately reply to an AP request for comment.

The toll reflected the rapid worsening of Yemen's civil war, where a years-long truce fell apart over the summer. Fighting has escalated between the Iranian-backed Houthis — who control Sanaa, the north, and the west of the country — and their Saudi-backed opponents based in the south and east.

On Friday (November 6, 2026), an airstrike in a market in southern Yemen killed at least 30 people, according to Houthi officials. The Houthis and Yemen's Saudi-backed military each blamed the other for that strike.

Footage from Houthi-run Al-Masirah TV of the aftermath of Saturday's (November 7, 2026) strikes showed staff carrying limp bodies of young children out of ambulances, bringing the casualties to a local hospital. One little girl's head had been cleaved open. Other children lay on stretchers, bloodied and bandaged as staff tended to them. Footage from the village showed the rubble of destroyed houses and dust filling the air as people hid in nearby agricultural fields.
Mr. Alasbahi said in a posting earlier on X that Saturday's (November 7, 2026) strikes hit several homes in al-Shariyah. Subsequent strikes targeted emergency responders, he told the AP .

In September, the Houthis made a lightning advance, capturing much of Yemen's Red Sea coast and strategic islands in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. They have also encircled the city of Taiz, a strategic gateway to southern Yemen. At the same time, they have stepped up strikes on Saudi Arabia, targeting oil and military infrastructure and shipping in the Red Sea.

articles.title: Iran says forces ‘stronger’ than at beginning of war
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Islamic Republic’s armed forces, having gained experience from direct confrontation with United States and Israel, are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war, Iranian Army Spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia said

Iran said Saturday (November 7, 2026) its military has grown "stronger" since the outset of its war with the United States, which has offered a $20 million reward for information about Tehran's nuclear programme.
Mediators have been working to prevent any resumption of fighting after months of deadlock in the West Asia conflict, which began when the United States and Israel attacked Iran in late February.
Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.
Iran says ready to reopen Hormuz in two days if U.S. agrees to demands
Iranian Army Spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia said Tehran retained control over the strategic waterway and that it would remain closed until its demands were met by the United States.
He also said Iran's forces had grown stronger and more confident, state news agency IRNA reported on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

"Today, the Islamic Republic's armed forces... having gained experience from direct confrontation with the United States and the Israeli regime, are on higher alert and are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war," he said.
"They now possess greater motivation, commitment, and self-confidence."
"Under the order of the Supreme Leader, the response of the armed forces will be immediate, effective, and without geographical limitations," he added.
On Friday (November 6, 2026), the U.S. military said it was offering a $20 million reward "and possible relocation" for information about Iran's nuclear programme.

Rewards for Justice, a U.S. State Department programme, was seeking information on topics including "facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community," U.S. Central Command said on X .
The programme was established in 1984 under the State Department's national security rewards programme to offer money for information that protects American lives and interests.

articles.title: No complete closure of Ballari Road for 18 months for elevated corridor work: BDA
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The clarification comes amid concerns over the traffic disruption expected during the construction period.

The Hebbal Flyover and Ballari Road corridor will not be completely closed for 18 months to facilitate the construction of the elevated corridor, the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) clarified on Saturday (November 7). Meanwhile, the Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP) said vehicular movement would continue with limited lane restrictions and phased traffic diversions.

The clarification comes amid concerns over the traffic disruption expected during the construction period. The elevated corridor is part of the BDA’s larger Integrated Tunnel and Elevated Corridor Project, aimed at easing congestion along the city’s crucial northern corridor connecting Bengaluru with Kempegowda International Airport. However, the project has also drawn considerable public criticism since it was announced.

The BTP sources said restrictions would apply only to the movement of heavy vehicles between 6 a.m. and 8 p.m., while other motorists would merely be “advised” to take alternative routes. Public transport vehicles and school buses would also be allowed to use the stretch.

The BDA said barricading would be restricted to a lane approximately 4.5 metres wide, affecting only one of the three existing lanes in each direction. The remaining two lanes and the service road would remain open to traffic.

The concern, however, is that the 4.5-metre-wide lane is part of one of the main carriageways and accounts for 35% of the traffic movement on the stretch at any given time. Consequently, the restrictions are likely to worsen congestion, irrespective of the timing of their implementation. At least 20% of the traffic will therefore need to be diverted to prevent gridlock along the stretch.
“Even without civic works, the stretch witnesses prolonged congestion during peak hours. So, with civic works, the need for traffic diversion is essential,” a police source said.

This makes the advisory to use alternative routes necessary. However, the identified alternate routes are also in poor condition. The BTP has now written to the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) and the BDA, requesting them to asphalt the alternative routes to ensure the smooth movement of vehicles and prevent congestion.

“Routes through New BEL Road and R.T. Nagar Station Road are among those being considered for improvement. Officials have also been asked to identify bottlenecks, improve road surfaces, and install adequate signage and road markings,” the BDA said.

articles.title: 'Tough' stance on Kishau Dam project laid ground for victory in BBMB dues case: Himachal CM
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu says he had consistently raised the issue of dues arising from BBMB projects and made it clear to the Centre that the rights of Himachal Pradesh in the matter must be resolved before any further progress was made on the Kishau Dam project

Hailing the Supreme Court verdict in the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB) arrears case, Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Saturday (November 7, 2026) said that the decision came in the State's favour on account of the "tough" stance his government took during discussions on the Kishau Dam project.

Mr. Sukhu said that during meetings with the Union Power Minister and officials, he had consistently raised the issue of dues arising from BBMB projects and made it clear that the rights of Himachal Pradesh in the matter must be resolved before any further progress was made on the Kishau Dam project.

He said the State asserted that it would not share the cost of the 440-MW Kishau Dam project, and the Haryana government assured that it would file an affidavit in the Supreme Court in favour of Himachal Pradesh for the release of arrears of its power share from BBMB projects.

Ruling in favour of Himachal Pradesh, the Supreme Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) said the hill State would get 11,973 MU of electricity from Punjab and Haryana over 20 years. The arrangement will be as per a 2011 Supreme Court verdict settling power dues arising out of Bhakra Nangal and Beas hydro projects since 1966 at the rate of 7.19%.

Talking to media persons here, Mr. Sukhu claimed that the case of arrears, pending for the past 15 years, would have taken many more years to decide if the government had not pursued it vigorously in the top court.

He said that the State government is exploring a better price to sell the electricity received from the BBMB. If the electricity is sold at the rate of ₹6 per unit, the State could earn around ₹500 crore, but the government is working towards securing a better power agreement that could increase the revenue to approximately ₹1,000 crore.

The Chief Minister said that the State government was moving ahead with the aim of making Himachal Pradesh self-reliant and expressed confidence that it would become the most prosperous State in the country by 2032.

articles.title: A woman stitches her way into the male-dominated ritual tradition of Theyyam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Based in Kannayi Mukkottu near Payyannur, she spends the Theyyam season creating attire and accessories, a craft she learned from her father and now sustains as a specialised, highly regarded artisan.

In the ritual world of Theyyam, where women rarely find a place in the traditional roles, 41-year-old M. Priya of Kannayi Mukkottu near Payyannur has carved out a distinctive space for herself. Rather than performing rituals, she stitches costumes and decorative garments that transforms male performers into divine figures in the Malabar’s sacred groves and temples.
For Priya, the Theyyam season is also the busiest time of the year. Beginning in November and continuing until March or May, depending on the festival calendar, it keeps her sewing machine busy.

Unlike conventional tailoring, Ms. Priya specialises exclusively in the traditional attire worn by Theyyam performers. She makes costumes and decorative accessories for almost all the Theyyam forms, following individual performances measurements and requirements.

“It takes nearly two days to stitch the complete costume for a Theyyam character. Each form has its own distinctive style of attire, requiring patience, precision, and an understanding of the traditional designs,” she said.

Ms. Priya’s learned the craft from her father, who stitched Theyyam costumes by hand before sewing machines became common. “I learned this by watching my father stitch the costumes at home. I developed an interest in this particular kind of stitching and gradually began doing it myself,” she said.

Although she has been involved in the work for over 15 years, Ms. Priya has never ventured into conventional tailoring. Performers from across Kannur and Kasargod districts approach her with their measurements and requirements.

Among the items she makes are kaani, kachunkaraa, Valinjery, kuttithaya and Velimban, Kayipodip, Thalachut besides several other components of Theyyam attire. Designs and stitching patterns vary according to the character, making each order a specialised assignment.

Orders pour in as the season approaches. Ms. Priya spends her evenings from 4 p.m. to 9 p.m. at the sewing machine. Her work has earned the appreciation of performers who depend on the precision and quality of their costumes.
Prashanth Panicker, who has been performing Theyyam since very young age, has been getting his costumes stitched by Ms. Priya.

“Stitching Theyyam costumes requires a great deal of patience. Once we get the costumes stitched by her, there is hardly any need to look elsewhere. The stitching is precise. I perform in several places in Kannur and Kasaragod, and her workmanship has become a familiar signature in the costumes I wear,” he says.
For Priya, the craft is not merely an occupation. Theyyam runs deep in her family. Her father was associated with the tradition, while her brothers children too have performed theyyam.

Her husband M Sashi has been a constant source of encouragement. An auto-rickshaw driver, he supports her work, helps her find customers and pursue her interest. He drives more more actively when the Theyyam season winds down.

articles.title: Enforcement Directorate is not a ‘super cop’, says Karnataka High Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ED cannot file private complaint when other agencies decline to act on its information on alleged offences, court said while quashing ED cases against K.Y. Nanjegowda, Congress MLA from Malur

In a setback to the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) , the High Court of Karnataka has held that the ED is “not a super cop” and cannot file a private complaint to initiate a money-laundering probe when the competent agencies decline to prosecute a scheduled offence based on the information filed by the ED.

The Court ruled that the ED’s power under the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act (PMLA) is “derivative and not original”, and that filing a private complaint under Section 200 Code of Criminal Procedure (Cr.P.C.) / Section 223 Bharatiya Nagarik Surakasha Sanhita is not contemplated under the PMLA Act.

“... one institution in the country does not become supreme so that it is in a position to abuse the powers conferred on it. Law recognises the requirements of checks and balances. The ED is not a super cop to investigate anything and everything which comes into its notice,” the Court observed, adding that the ED must exercise only those powers expressly conferred on it by the PMLA.

Justice M.I. Arun passed the order while allowing a batch of writ petitions filed by Congress Party MLA from Malur constituency K.Y. Nanjegowda, who is also Chairman of the Kolar and Chikkaballapur Milk Union Ltd. (KOMUL), Y.B. Ashwathanarayana then Director of KOMUL, K.N. Gopala Murthy, Nagesh N. and Raju Krishna C.

The petitioners had challenged the ED’s ECIR registered in November 2023, the Adjudicating Authority’s order confirming seizure of articles, summons issued to them, and the private complaint filed by the ED before a special court.

The case stemmed from the criminal proceedings initiated based on a private complaint on “land scam” lodged by one K.C. Rajanna before a trial court in Kolar alleging irregularities in the grant of about 80 acres of land to 38 persons by the Malur Land Grant Committee, of which Mr. Nanjegowda was chairman.

Treating this case it as a predicate offence, the ED had registered ECIR in 2023. During searches conducted based in this ECIR, the ED agency claimed to have stumbled upon material indicating irregularities in recruitments to the KOMUL, which it termed a separate “job scam.” Further, the ED had shared with the Karnataka Lokayukta police the information on alleged “job scam” that it had discovered during the searches.

However, the “land scam” case ended in a closure report by the jurisdictional police, and the trial court dismissed it for want of sanction to prosecute a public servant even though complainant Mr. Rajanna protested against closure report.

As the Lokayukta police did not act on the information shared by it under Section 66(2) of the PMLA), the ED itself had filed a private complaint before a special court in Bengaluru on KOMUL “job scam.”

It was argued on behalf of the petitioners that once the predicate offence collapses, even on technical grounds, the ED cannot continue PMLA proceedings, and that when ED uncovers a different scheduled offence, its only permissible course is to share information with the competent agency and not filing a separate private complaint and probe it.
Accepting petitioners’ contentions, the Court held that Section 66(2) casts a duty on the ED to intimate the concerned agency, not to take up the investigation itself.

“In law, where an act is to be done in a particular way, it must be done in that way and in no other way,” the Court said, invoking the constitutional separation of powers and the need for checks and balances.

articles.title: Manipur gets Northeast’s first AI-enabled career intelligence hub
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh says the facility marks a significant step towards integrating artificial intelligence into the education and career guidance ecosystem of the State
Conflict-scarred Manipur has become the first State in the northeastern region to get an artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled facility that aims to mould careers.

Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh on Saturday (November 7, 2026) inaugurated the AI-enabled Career Intelligence Hub at the Tamphasana Girls’ Higher Secondary School in Imphal, the State’s capital.

Established under the Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme as the region’s first-of-its-kind facility, the initiative marked a “significant step towards integrating AI into the education and career guidance ecosystem in the State”.
The Chief Minister said the government undertook the initiative to provide students with technology-driven career guidance, personalised counselling, and information on emerging career opportunities.

He commended students who focused on their education and future instead of participating in agitations over the past few months, advising others to pursue dialogue as the preferred means of resolving any differences and addressing critical issues.
“AI has advanced significantly and is increasingly transforming various fields and professions,” he said, underscoring the need for students to upgrade for the career challenges ahead.

Earlier, the Chief Minister lauded two districts—Imphal West and Pherzawl—for achieving ‘ surakshit (safe)’ status in October under the National AIDS Control Organisation’s (NACO) Mobilisation for AIDS Suraksha initiative.

“This achievement means that 95% of the estimated number of people living with Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) in a district are aware of their status, 95% of those aware of their status are receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART), and 95% of those undergoing ART have achieved viral suppression,” he said.

articles.title: Rampur’s Lavi Fair: Storytelling through 300 years of Himalayan trade and tradition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Rampur Bushahr’s Lavi Fair in Himachal Pradesh traces a Himalayan journey from wool and barter to women entrepreneurs and digital payments

What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

For a few weeks, Rampur, on the banks of the Sutlej river, comes alive with the fair (November 11-14 this year, with trading grounds open through the month), offering a sensory map of the Himalaya. Colourful textiles, yak wool, pashmina, dry fruits, agricultural produce, Kinnauri apples, indigenous crafts and precious stones fill the marketplace. Among its most captivating sights are the magnificent Chamurthi horses, the hardy “ships of the cold desert”.
Kinnauri weaves on sale at Lavi Fair. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala
At the Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, Shimla district. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala
Jewellery on sale at Lavi Fair. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala

Traders once travelled from Tibet, Nepal, Central Asia and Afghanistan. Tradition traces the fair’s origins to a 17th-century treaty between Raja Kehri Singh of Bushahr and Tibet, establishing it as a meeting point for traders, pilgrims and storytellers along the Silk Route. Though trans-Himalayan trade declined after Tibet’s occupation in 1959, the fair survived on the Buddhist circuit and was accorded international status by the Himachal Pradesh government.

Pratibha Singh, a member of the Rampur Bushahr royal family which founded the fair and continues to honour the tradition, recalls its legacy of pashmina and Kinnauri shawls, some woven over years, alongside trans-Himalayan textiles and local produce. The GI-tagged Kinnauri shawl, with bright geometric motifs, speaks its own language of colour: white for water, yellow for earth, red for fire, green for air, and blue for sky.

On my last visit, a group of elderly women from South India told me they discovered the fair through a fellow traveller whose husband was a biker in the 1990s. A friend from Odisha recalls how in the 90s, his ophthalmologist-father’s eye camps in Rampur led to lifelong friendships and an annual habit of sourcing Kinnauri apples and dry fruits.
Kinnauri apples on sale at Lavi Fair. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala
Traders at Lavi Fair accept payments via UPI now. | Photo Credit: Nitika Kuthiala

For Ami Chand Gautam, a Lavi trader since the 1980s, the fair tells a story of changing prices and livelihoods. He remembers when “ chilgoza , the rare pine nut gathered in Kinnaur’s upper reaches, sold for just ₹4-₹5 per kg, almost the price of rice then. Today, it fetches ₹14,000-15,000 per kg,” he says.

articles.title: VISTAR: India’s shift towards a real-time, technology-driven statistical system | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: For an economy aspiring to become a developed nation by 2047, the statistical blind spots could translate into costly policy mistakes, misdirected investments and ineffective welfare schemes

India’s statistical requirements have outgrown the conventional survey-based architecture, requiring a more scientific and technological architecture to better capture key performance indicators of economy, even as it should avoid the growing risks of synthetic data.

Seeking to move official data collection beyond periodic surveys and administrative records, the VISTAR or Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research is a major overhaul of India’s official statistical system at the centre and state levels using interoperable datasets, bridging data gaps and generating timely, reliable socioeconomic indicators for evidence-based policymaking.

articles.title: Heavy rain inundates shelters for people displaced by war in Gaza
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: In a statement, the Hamas-run government media office said that about "70,000 tents sheltering tens of thousands of displaced people were flooded on the first day" of rains
Heavy rain on Saturday (November 7, 2026) flooded tens of thousands of displaced people's tents in war-devastated Gaza, Palestinian authorities said, leaving them without shelter.
In a statement, the Hamas-run government media office said that about "70,000 tents sheltering tens of thousands of displaced people were flooded on the first day" of rains.
It also noted the "collapse of dozens of cracked walls and roofs, which caused injuries", some critical, in various areas of the tiny territory.

Since early Saturday (November 7, 2026), hundreds of displaced families have been seen fleeing camps in parts of Gaza City and in the central and northern areas of the Strip after they were inundated by rainwater.

Civil defence spokesman Mahmoud Bassal told AFP his teams had received more than 1,500 calls during the night from residents requesting urgent assistance after their tents were flooded, explaining that the agency "is operating without any equipment or capabilities".

"We have issued an urgent distress call to the international community and humanitarian organisations to intervene immediately to save hundreds of thousands of displaced people from the flooding of their tents."
"We cannot face the consequences of this storm on our own."

Um Muhammad al-Hersh, 45, who lives with her family in a tent in western Gaza, told AFP, "We were not able to save the mattresses, and all the clothes were soaked. Our suffering is repeated every winter."
Maryam Odeh, 34, who lives with her children in Deir al-Balah, said, "We no longer know how to protect our children. My children ask me where we will sleep tonight, and I have no answer".
For his part, Khaled al-Najjar, 41, said, "We fear for our children not only from the flooding of the tents, but also from the cold and the widespread diseases".

A coalition of Palestinian civil society organisations warned in a statement of "the catastrophe that has come to threaten the lives of hundreds of thousands of residents", pointing to the risk of the spread of diseases and epidemics.
The coalition, which includes dozens of local institutions and organisations, called for "pressure on Israel to allow the entry of humanitarian aid without restrictions".

articles.title: Ukraine says Russia ramps up strikes to pressure Kyiv at talks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Ukraine's Energy Ministry said "a massive attack on a number of energy facilities" had plunged five regions into darkness and significantly hampered electricity transmission in Kyiv and surrounding region

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Saturday (November 7, 2026) accused Russia of intensifying strikes across the country to put pressure on Kyiv at upcoming talks after an overnight barrage triggered power cuts as temperatures drop.

The latest strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure came days before the trilateral U.S.-brokered meeting in Abu Dhabi scheduled for Tuesday (November 10, 2026) and Wednesday (November 11, 2026), aimed at reviving stalled diplomatic efforts towards peace.

Ukraine's Energy Ministry said "a massive attack on a number of energy facilities" had plunged five regions into darkness and significantly hampered electricity transmission in Kyiv and surrounding region.

Mr. Zelenskyy said the timing of the aerial barrage showed that Russia had a "very particular view of diplomacy" as it struck ahead of "another joint effort with our partners to reinvigorate negotiations".

"By intensifying its attacks on Ukraine and our infrastructure at this very moment, Russia is trying to lay the groundwork for putting pressure on Ukraine's position and that of its partners," Mr. Zelenskyy said.

Moscow has battered Ukraine's energy grid and infrastructure throughout its four-and-a-half-year invasion, and Kyiv is now bracing for another harsh winter as temperatures begin to hover around freezing.
Mr. Zelenskyy also said Russia had, throughout the night, launched 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles, among which, according to him, were KN-23 missiles manufactured and supplied by North Korea.
They hit "one of the key energy facilities that was damaged", Mr. Zelenskyy said.
Russia has turned to North Korea for support throughout invasion.
Earlier in the war, Pyongyang dispatched thousands of troops to help Russia fight back a Ukrainian counterattack in its western Kursk region.

The Russian Defence Ministry in a statement on Saturday (November 7, 2026) said it had struck "facilities belonging to the military-industrial complex, the energy sector, and transport infrastructure" in Kyiv and its surrounding region.
Mr. Zelenskyy urged the United States to increase its flagging aid to Ukraine.

articles.title: Abdul El-Sayed: The progressive’s progress
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Abdul El-Sayed’s describes himself as ‘just a capitalist who understands how capitalism works’ and identifies as a progressive; his candidacy was backed by leading figures such as Bernie Sanders and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez

In a country where, for more than a quarter of a century, the word “Muslim” has been used as an accusation in politics, Abdul El-Sayed’s election as the first Muslim member of the U.S. Senate breaks perhaps the thickest of glass ceilings in American public life. Dr. El-Sayed, a physician and epidemiologist, defeated the Republican former Congressman Mike Rogers with 52.5% of the vote, seven percentage points ahead of his rival.

It would be easy to dismiss this victory as merely a byproduct of the “blue wave” in the U.S. midterms, which carried Democratic candidates to wins even in Republican strongholds such as South Carolina, Texas, and Kansas. But that would be a reductive reading. The odds Dr. El-Sayed faced make the win remarkable in its own right.

articles.title: As COP31 comes to Turkiye, satellites reveal a landfill methane problem
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Methane is the biggest cause of climate change after carbon dioxide (CO2) and is over 80 times more potent than CO2 in its first 20 years in the air. Sharp cuts could therefore slow warming relatively quickly

In the countryside west ​of Istanbul, trucks line up to empty mixed household waste from the city of 16 million people onto a vast landscape of decomposing rubbish, where landfill gas is captured to ‌generate electricity at a nearby plant.
But far above the seagulls circling the waste, satellites detect what the plant has failed to ​capture: methane escaping at a rate that ranks it among the world’s largest recorded landfill emitters.
Turkiye hosts COP31 in Antalya from November ⁠9 to 20 and has made methane reduction a priority for the climate summit.

Methane is the biggest cause of climate change after carbon dioxide (CO2) and is over 80 times more potent than CO2 in its first 20 years in the air. Sharp cuts could therefore slow warming relatively quickly.
Turkiye’s waste sector illustrates both the potential and the difficulty of achieving rapid ‌cuts.
The country is the world’s fifth-biggest emitter of methane from solid waste behind China, the United States, Russia and Brazil, according to data from non-profit emissions tracker Climate TRACE.

Satellite observations analysed by researchers at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) identified 70 plumes from Turkiye’s 10 highest-emitting ‌waste sites, where average detected rates ranged from 841 kg to 7.4 metric tons an hour. Three were around Istanbul, while others were near Ankara, Izmir ‌and ⁠Antalya, where COP31 is being held.
Gas capture is widespread at Turkiye’s larger municipal landfills, indicating that collection systems alone do not prevent ⁠large releases.

Tia Scarpelli, waste sector lead for emissions-monitoring non-profit Carbon Mapper, said cutting landfill methane requires diverting organic material before it reaches dumps, while improving rates of capture.
Because Turkiye’s largest detected emissions were concentrated at a few sites, addressing those landfills could deliver disproportionate gains, Scarpelli said.

“There is this huge mitigation potential by just addressing the largest landfills to reduce their national emissions,” she said, suggesting ​better-designed collection systems and repairs to cracked covers or faulty gas wells.
The ‌UCLA analysis used public Carbon Mapper data from the Tanager-1 satellite between January 2025 and end-May 2026.

articles.title: Rajajingar murders: How did the accused transport bodies across locations without being caught?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Neither a patrolling vehicle nor a checkpoint caught the accused Indushekhar even as he crossed State borders

At least three trips with seven bodies in the car to four different locations, and one of them an inter-State journey. Yet, the accused in the alleged Rajajinagar murders, Indushekhar, was never detected. This has raised questions about the effectiveness of the nakabandi (checkpoints) and night patrolling system in the city.

Indushekar, prime accused in the case where he killed his wife and six others from her family , resided in a building near (barely 100 metres) the famous Bhashyam Circle in Rajajinagar. The junction is barely 3 km from Majestic, the city’s transport hub. It connects to Chord Road, one of the major roads in the city. The junction also provides connectivity between the central, western and southern parts of Bengaluru.
The accused allegedly brought the bodies down from the second floor and transported them to Mysuru, deep into the Western Ghats (Shiradi Ghat), to the Tamil Nadu border and to Chickballapur.

The alleged incidents unfolded over 15 days. Neither a patrolling vehicle nor a checkpoint detected the accused, even as he crossed State borders. The development comes amid frequent police checks at night across the city. In several instances, there have also been allegations of harassment during such checks.
A senior police officer told The Hindu that the accused’s movement with bodies in the car was among the questions on their investigation list, though it was not their immediate focus.

“A team has already been deployed to recreate all the movements of the accused and gather footage of his movements after October 16. We will verify whether he passed any checkpoints in the city and whether there was any negligence on the part of officers,” he said.
The officer stressed that the immediate focus was on recovering the bodies, as they were the prime evidence in the case. Any dereliction of duty could be investigated at a later stage.

The officer further said that they suspect the accused deliberately avoided stretches where checkpoints were set up. “We must also consider that all vehicles are checked at checkpoints. He may have passed through one,” the officer added.

“We also suspect that he avoided toll plazas. For a person who meticulously planned how to clean the crime scene thoroughly, he must have planned the routes in advance and executed the disposals accordingly,” the officer said.

The officer also pointed to a murder cover-up in a case reported in C.K. Acchukattu in 2025. The body was found dumped in a garbage pile. However, the accused had transported it from Madiwala to C.K. Acchukattu. What was even more surprising was that the accused had carried the body alone on a scooter.

“Only when we interrogated the accused did we get to know that he had deliberately avoided routes with police checkpoints,” the officer said, adding that there had been several such instances in the past.

Similarly, the family of Nalini, one of the victims in the present case, alleged that the Srirampura police initially refused to register a missing-person complaint on November 1. It was registered only on November 3.

fullParagraphs: Students should dare to dream big, think independently and pursue ambitious goals to drive innovation and contribute to the vision of a self-reliant India, said Prof. Ramesh Srikonda, Director of the School of Planning and Architecture, Vijayawada.

Addressing the Freshers’ Day celebrations at Dr. RVR NRI Institute of Technology (Deemed to be University), he emphasised that bold aspirations lead to new ideas and innovative outcomes. He urged students to focus on holistic development rather than limiting their ambitions to obtaining academic degrees.

The celebrations, organised to welcome newly admitted first-year students, witnessed the participation of over 2,000 students, who showcased their talents through colourful singing and dancing performances.

Prof. M.L.N. Rao, Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor of Rajiv Gandhi University of Knowledge Technologies (RGUKT-AP), said emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Quantum Technologies would drive major transformations over the next five to 10 years. He encouraged students to prepare themselves to contribute to the visions of Swarna Andhra Pradesh 2047 and Viksit Bharat 2047.

NRI University Chairman and Chancellor Dr. Ravi Venkata Rao said the institution’s four-year academic programme aimed at shaping students into responsible, capable individuals equipped to overcome challenges and contribute meaningfully to society.

Vice-Chancellor Dr. K.R.S. Sambasiva Rao urged students to make effective use of the university’s teaching and learning facilities and continuously upgrade their skills to become industry-ready professionals.
Organising convener and Dean D. Suneetha, CEO, Pro-Vice-Chancellors, Registrar, Deans, Heads of Departments, faculty members and other dignitaries attended the celebrations.

articles.title: Bengaluru’s GBA launches phase 2 of ‘Ward One’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda on Saturday directed officials to prepare a comprehensive plan for the redevelopment of the K.R. Puram-Tin Factory Junction. The plan should focus on pedestrian safety, public transport integration and smoother traffic movement, he said.

The directions came during the launch of the second phase of the ‘Ward One’ campaign. The second phase has been launched across around 40 wards. The first phase covered 43 wards, with nearly 90% of the identified works completed, Mr. Gowda said.

On Saturday, the Minister inspected the K.R. Puram-Tin Factory Junction and reviewed the problems from ongoing metro and K-RIDE works and the pedestrian infrastructure, following which directions were issued.

The plan would be prepared jointly by the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA), Namma Metro officials, and Janaagraha, he said. The plan would cover road design, footpaths, bus bays, bus stops and traffic management. The Minister also called for scientifically redesigning the junction, improving road curves, and providing free left turns wherever necessary.

He directed metro officials to restore roads affected by the construction without delay. “Potholes on connecting roads must be repaired within a week. Roads at lower levels, which are prone to flooding, also need to be improved,” he told officials.
The campaign brings together various civic agencies to address potholes, damaged footpaths, garbage accumulation, construction waste, streetlights and drain desilting.

articles.title: Habitual offender arrested for murdering 65-year-old woman in Bengaluru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Kengeri police have arrested a habitual offender for allegedly murdering a 65-year-old woman who was sleeping outside a temple and robbing her of cash and a gold ring in Vrushabhavathi Nagar Layout.
The deceased, Narayanamma, was found dead in front of the Pataladamma Temple at Vrushabhavathi Nagar Layout, Konasandra, within Kengeri police station limits, on November 3.
According to the police, Narayanamma had left her house due to family problems and had been sleeping outside the temple for the past few days.
A local resident who noticed her body informed her son, who arrived at the spot and identified her. The Kengeri police initially registered an unnatural death report based on his complaint.

However, following the post-mortem examination and information gathered during the investigation, police suspected that she had been murdered and robbed. A murder case was subsequently registered on Thursday.
During the investigation, police apprehended a suspicious person moving around Vrushabhavathi Nagar Layout on Friday. During interrogation, he allegedly confessed to the crime.
The accused reportedly told investigators that he had noticed Narayanamma sleeping alone and decided to rob her to arrange money to fund his vices.
In the early hours of November 3, he allegedly went to the spot, covered her mouth, assaulted her and robbed her of the cash she was carrying and a gold ring before fleeing, leaving her dead.

Police said the accused has a criminal history and was previously involved in cases registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act and robbery cases at Girinagar and Cottonpet police stations.
Further investigation and interrogation are under way, police said.

articles.title: From poverty alleviation to prosperity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: India has reduced extreme poverty, but its high prosperity gap shows that millions remain far from a comfortable standard of living; informal work, stagnant wages and limited employment opportunities continue to constrain upward mobility

From the poverty income ruler line provided by the recent World Bank estimates, India has recorded one of the fastest extreme income-poverty declines in the world, as per its latest Poverty and Equity brief, which highlights that between 2011 and 2023, an estimated 496 million people moved out of poverty, with extreme income-based poverty ($3/per day) declining to 2.6%.

For the same period, the share of the population living below the lower middle-income country line ($4.20/day, 2021 PPP) fell from 57.7% to 16.1%. Non-monetary poverty indicators, as per OPHI’s Multi-dimensional Poverty Index, also recorded a sharp reduction in overall poverty numbers, i.e., from 53.8% in 2005-06 to 16.4% in 2019-21.

articles.title: Festivals, infections and more | Health Wrap Ep. 58
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: In the 58th episode of Health Wrap by The Hindu, Ramya Kannan, Health Editor, The Hindu, and Zubeda Hamid, Senior Assistant Editor, The Hindu, discuss the public health concerns surrounding festivals, marking Diwali, including air pollution and AQI

On Diwali day, as India celebrates the festival of lights, and firecrackers dazzle and explode, it’s perhaps timely to talk about health concerns related to festivals as well. The issue gains relevance, given that Delhi is already reeling under severe air pollution levels

In the 58th episode of Health Wrap by The Hindu, Ramya Kannan, Health Editor, The Hindu, and Zubeda Hamid, Senior Assistant Editor, The Hindu, discuss the public health concerns surrounding festivals, marking Diwali, including air pollution and AQI. Air pollution is now longer just a respiratory concern - research is increasingly linking it to several other health concerns including diabetes, heart disease and cancer. How to stay safe during both festive seasons, and all year around, are, therefore, important discussions to have.

With Ebola continuing to rage in parts of Africa, and the first death of a child in New York State of measles in 30 years, the issue of controlling the spread of infectious diseases has once again come into focus. Do watch for insights into how a One Health approach, which prioritises human, animal health, is the way forward, along with global cooperation and collaboration to tackling infectious diseases. And let’s not forget that vaccination remains crucial, and vital tool in our armamentarium.

Despite decades of progress, India still hasn’t fully been able to ensure quality maternal and child health care for all. Recent deaths of infants in tribal communities in Attapady, Keralam, have been in the news, calling for a deeper look at just why anaemia and malnutrition persist, and what interventions are needed to help tackle these issues.
The video also features a discussion on new research into Hepatitis B.

articles.title: Willem Einthoven’s Nobel-winning discovery that laid the foundations of the modern ECG
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Willem Einthoven’s development of the string galvanometer transformed the recording of cardiac electrical signals and laid the foundations of modern electrocardiography
In 1924, Dutch physician and physiologist Willem Einthoven was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine “for his discovery of the mechanism of the electrocardiogram (ECG)”.

His work made it possible to record the electrical activity of the heart with greater accuracy. By developing the string galvanometer and establishing a standard method for interpreting its recordings, Einthoven helped turn electrocardiography into an important tool for studying heart function. Today, the ECG is routinely used to investigate irregular heart rhythms, detect signs of reduced blood supply to the heart muscle and identify evidence of previous heart attacks.

Science, Space & Environment Report: Willem Einthoven’s Nobel-winning discovery that laid the foundations of the modern ECG. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

His work made it possible to record the electrical activity of the heart with greater accuracy. By developing the string galvanometer and establishing a standard method for interpreting its recordings, Einthoven helped turn electrocardiography into an important tool for studying heart function. Today, the ECG is routinely used to investigate irregular heart rhythms, detect signs of reduced blood supply to the heart muscle and identify evidence of previous heart attacks.

In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh , cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases.
